topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-aware deep models in AL
topic_metadata.description: This topic covers deep models that inherently model predictive distributions rather than point estimates, such as VAEs and probabilistic U-Nets. These models output full distributions over predictions, reducing over-confidence compared to deterministic networks and providing built-in uncertainty estimates. They require only a single forward pass at inference, lowering computational and time costs for active learning pipelines.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Multi-label EDL using Beta distributions
topic_metadata.description: In multi-label chest X-ray classification, EDL is adapted by decomposing the Dirichlet distribution into multiple Beta distributions, one per class label. Each Beta distribution models the evidential uncertainty for a specific label, and its entropy is used as the aleatoric uncertainty metric for annotation. This enables uncertainty-aware active learning in a multi-label medical imaging setting.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: EDL-based active domain adaptation
topic_metadata.description: Here, EDL is employed within an active domain adaptation framework to select samples under both data and distributional uncertainty. Samples exhibiting high distribution uncertainty (domain shift) and high data uncertainty are prioritized for annotation. This evidential approach tailors active learning to settings where source and target data distributions differ.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: KL-divergence-driven adversarial attacks for uncertainty
topic_metadata.description: Here, adversarial attacks are constructed by maximizing the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between the model’s predictions on original and perturbed inputs under a bounded perturbation norm. The KL divergence quantifies how much the prediction distribution changes under small adversarial noise, capturing local sensitivity of the classifier. Samples for which this divergence is maximized, given the perturbation constraint, are deemed more uncertain and are selected for annotation. This leverages distributional disagreement under adversarial perturbations as an uncertainty metric.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Adversarial training with classifier disagreement
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes an adversarial training scheme that alternates optimization of a shared feature extractor and multiple classifiers to surface uncertain samples. Two classifiers are trained on labeled and unlabeled data: first, classifiers are updated while the feature extractor is fixed to increase disagreement and expose ambiguous regions; next, the feature extractor is updated against fixed classifiers to reduce the discrepancy between labeled and unlabeled representations. After several alternations, samples that induce the largest classifier disagreements are identified as most informative and are annotated. The method combines adversarial objectives in representation learning with disagreement-based active learning.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Distribution Misalignment and Dataset Bias
topic_metadata.description: In feature space, uncertain samples tend to lie near the decision boundary, so uncertainty-based selection skews the queried set toward this region. As a result, the distribution of queried samples diverges from the overall data distribution, introducing dataset bias. This misalignment can cause a performance drop and motivates considering relationships among samples during querying.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting with '2. Distribution misalignment' through 'could be alleviated... during the AL query.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Limitations of Uncertainty as Informativeness Metric
topic_metadata.description: Uncertainty-based AL under-exploits the visual content of each sample and the inter-sample relationships, focusing instead on model confidence alone. This limitation leads to outlier selection and distribution misalignment. Consequently, the authors argue for designing new informativeness metrics that explicitly encode sample characteristics and their relationships.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences beginning 'In summary, uncertainty-based AL lacks exploration...' through 'call for a new informativeness metric in AL.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Feature Representations in Medical Image AL
topic_metadata.description: Medical images are high-dimensional and contain complex, often non-obvious information about lesions, tissues, and anatomical or functional structures. Good feature representations lower dimensionality while encoding anatomical, histological, pathological, and functional cues relevant to clinical tasks. Because of this, representativeness-based querying is typically executed in the learned feature space rather than raw image space.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences beginning 'In medical image analysis, images are often high-dimensional...' through 'Therefore, the query process of representativeness-based AL is often conducted in the feature space.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Clustering-based active learning framework
topic_metadata.description: Clustering-based active learning exploits the fact that similar medical images cluster together in feature space, enabling selection of representative samples via clustering on embeddings. Data are partitioned into clusters and cluster centroids are chosen for annotation, leveraging the data’s inherent structure while remaining easy to implement. This provides a straightforward query strategy that focuses labeling effort on diverse, representative points.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening part of section: from 'With the advancement of feature extraction...' through 'K-Means was the most popular choice in clustering-based active learning.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Coarse-to-fine clustering for nuclei segmentation
topic_metadata.description: Lou et al. propose a two-level clustering strategy using K-Means for nuclei segmentation in pathological images. They first perform coarse-level clustering to broadly group patches and then fine-level clustering within these groups to refine selection. The goal is to identify particularly informative image patches for labeling, improving segmentation quality while keeping annotation costs low.
topic_metadata.text_span: middle of section: sentences 'In nuclei segmentation, Lou et al. (2023) performed coarse-level and fine-level clustering using K-Means, aiming to select informative patches from pathological images.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Active learning via ROI correctness judgment
topic_metadata.description: In connectomics, Lin et al. first predict a semantic mask for each unlabeled sample and then reformulate active learning as judging whether each predicted region of interest (ROI) is correct. This shifts the labeling task from full annotation to verification of model-generated segmentations. The approach narrows annotation to critical ROIs where model predictions may be unreliable, increasing efficiency.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Two-stream VAE-based clustering in connectomics
topic_metadata.description: Lin et al. train two separate feature extractors based on variational autoencoders (VAEs): one on segmentation masks and another on unlabeled images. These two streams provide complementary feature spaces for clustering in active learning. In particular, they apply mask-level clustering using mask features to group ROIs with similar appearances, guiding selection of diverse and uncertain regions for annotation in connectomics.

topic_metadata.title: Hierarchical mask and image-level clustering
topic_metadata.description: The approach first forms clusters based on segmentation masks and then performs additional clustering at the image level within each mask cluster. This hierarchical strategy separates structural (mask-based) similarity from broader visual (image-based) similarity. Such a design aims to better capture fine-grained object-level patterns before aggregating image-level characteristics. It is particularly suitable for medical images where object shape and appearance both carry diagnostic information.

topic_metadata.title: Two-stream clustering vs feature concatenation
topic_metadata.description: Two-stream clustering processes mask features and image features in separate streams, instead of concatenating them into a single feature vector. The results indicate that this separation prevents image features from overwhelming the contribution of mask features during clustering. As a consequence, structural information encoded in masks is preserved, leading to more balanced and meaningful clusters. This highlights the importance of feature-stream decoupling in multi-modal or multi-feature clustering setups.

topic_metadata.title: Application to synapse and mitochondria analysis
topic_metadata.description: The described clustering method is applied to tasks such as synapse detection and mitochondria segmentation in medical images. These are fine-scale, structure-focused problems where accurate delineation and recognition of small biological entities are critical. The method achieves excellent performance on these tasks, suggesting that its design is well-suited to capturing the complex shapes and appearances of subcellular structures. This demonstrates the utility of advanced clustering strategies in biomedical image analysis.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences 2–3: 'This method achieved excellent performance in synapse detection and mitochondria segmentation.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Cover-based representativeness in active learning
topic_metadata.description: Cover-based active learning casts representativeness as a covering problem in feature space, analogous to placing spheres whose centers are selected samples to cover all data points. Two main formulations are discussed: set cover, which enforces complete coverage of the dataset, and maximum cover, which aims to cover as much as possible without strict completeness. Both are NP-hard but admit near-optimal greedy solutions that iteratively pick samples covering the largest number of remaining points. The trade-offs include large radii and outlier selection risk under set cover, versus more flexible coverage and reduced outlier bias under maximum cover.
topic_metadata.text_span: Opening paragraphs describing covering problem, spheres in feature space, set cover vs maximum cover, and NP-hardness with greedy solutions (up to 'avoiding the issue of outlier selection.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Maximum-cover-based Segmentation Active Learning (SA)
topic_metadata.description: Segmentation Active learning (SA) is an early representativeness-based method that first queries highly uncertain samples and then selects representative ones under a maximum cover formulation. Representativeness of an unlabeled sample is defined via cosine similarity to its most similar queried sample, and a global representativeness score sums these over all unlabeled samples. SA uses a greedy strategy to add points that maximally increase this representativeness measure, effectively generalizing the discrete maximum cover problem to continuous similarities in [0,1]. This framework became a foundation for many later cover-based active learning approaches in medical image analysis.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph beginning 'Maximum cover: As a pioneering work of AL in medical image analysis, SA (Yang et al., 2017)...' through the equations (10) and (11) and greedy maximization description

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Medical imaging extensions of SA-style maximum cover
topic_metadata.description: Several works extend the SA maximum-cover framework to diverse medical image tasks by modifying feature extraction, similarity measures, or the selection protocol. Examples include quantizing segmentation networks to improve accuracy and reduce memory, using VAEs with hierarchical clustering to define clusters and select representative points per cluster (RA), and inverting the similarity measure to 1−sim(·,·) to emphasize diversity in breast cancer segmentation. Other variants use self-supervised feature extractors and SIFT-based keypoints to select template images with maximal average cosine similarity for few-shot keypoint detection, or shift from set cover to maximum cover with graph-based greedy algorithms (ProbCover) to avoid outlier selection. Collectively, these methods illustrate how representativeness via maximum cover is adapted to segmentation, detection, and few-shot scenarios in medical imaging.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraphs describing Xu et al. (2018), Zheng et al. (2019) RA, Shen et al. (2020), Quan et al. (2022), and Yehuda et al. (2022) ProbCover, following the SA description

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Submodular formulations for cover-based active learning
topic_metadata.description: Set cover and maximum cover objectives can be expressed with submodular set functions, which exhibit diminishing returns: the marginal gain of adding an element decreases as the selected set grows. When an informativeness function I is monotone and submodular, greedy selection of samples that maximize the marginal gain in I yields near-optimal solutions in linear time, naturally modeling the idea that earlier queries should be most informative. Although methods like SA and RA were not explicitly framed this way, their objectives align with submodular formulations that encourage both representativeness and diversity. Typical pipelines involve computing pairwise similarities, defining a submodular objective over candidate subsets, and solving it greedily.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting 'View of submodular functions: Both set cover and maximum cover...' through the discussion of informativeness function I and generic steps for submodular AL

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Similarity-based distribution discrepancy metrics
topic_metadata.description: Similarity-based discrepancy approximates distribution distance via pairwise sample similarity, such as average cosine similarity between feature vectors from labeled and unlabeled sets. In medical segmentation tasks, samples far from the labeled set and close to the unlabeled set are selected, while graph-based methods like UncertainGCN use GCNs to model sample relationships and pick unlabeled nodes with lowest similarity to labeled ones. Prototype-based object detection methods build class or feature prototypes (sometimes incorporating prediction entropy) and query samples far from these labeled prototypes.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraph beginning with 'Similarity-based discrepancy:' through the description of Li and Yin (2020), Caramalau et al. (2021), and Wu et al. (2022a)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Extensions of adversarial discrepancy-based AL
topic_metadata.description: Several methods extend VAAL by modifying the representation, supervision signal, or discriminator architecture to enhance active learning. Multimodal variants adapt the VAE to reconstruct multiple medical image modalities from a single-modality latent code, enabling cross-modal consistency in tasks such as brain tumor segmentation and chest X-ray classification. Other works remove adversarial training, replace binary discriminator labels with sample uncertainty, combine VAE and supervised-model features, or add extra discriminators distinguishing real from VAE-reconstructed features so that selection modules favor both uncertain and representative samples. Additional hybrids feed learning-loss predictions together with VAE features into the discriminator to enrich the selection signal.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraphs starting from 'VAAL inspired many subsequent works.' through the descriptions of Khanal et al. (2023), Gissin and Shalev-Shwartz (2019), Zhang et al. (2020), Wang et al. (2020c), and Kim et al. (2021)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Optimal transport and continuous candidate selection
topic_metadata.description: Some methods formalize active learning as an optimal transport problem that minimizes the Wasserstein distance between labeled and unlabeled sets using self-supervised feature representations. Mixed-integer programming is employed to guarantee globally convergent and diverse sample selection, ensuring a well-spread labeled set in feature space. Other approaches treat candidate points as continuous variables in feature space, optimizing them to be close to unlabeled neighbors and far from labeled samples, then querying the nearest real samples; this optimization objective is shown to be equivalent to minimizing the Wasserstein distance.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraphs describing Mahmood et al. (2022) and Xie et al. (2023b), starting from 'Mahmood et al. (2022) formulated AL as an optimal transport problem.' through the equivalence to minimizing the Wasserstein distance

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: MMD and taxonomy of discrepancy measures
topic_metadata.description: Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) quantifies the distance between two distributions as the difference between their kernel-mean embeddings, effectively comparing mean feature representations in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. In active domain adaptation, MMD is used to measure the distance between source and target domains and to select target samples that are simultaneously representative and diverse. The section also clarifies that Wasserstein distance belongs to the family of integral probability metrics (IPM), while MMD belongs both to IPM and to the broader category related to H-divergence, and references external work for a more detailed taxonomy of such discrepancy measures.
topic_metadata.text_span: final paragraph starting from 'Maximum mean discrepancy measures the distance...' to the end of the section

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: InfoVAE-based density estimation for MRI AL
topic_metadata.description: In shoulder MRI musculoskeletal segmentation, infoVAE is used to estimate sample density for both labeled and unlabeled sets. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) replaces KL divergence as the regularization term during training, and the encoder’s posterior probability serves as the density metric. Samples with high density relative to the unlabeled pool but low density relative to the labeled dataset are prioritized for annotation, balancing representativeness and novelty.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting with 'In shoulder MRI musculoskeletal segmentation, Ozdemir et al. (2021)' through 'were selected for annotation.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Fixed-representation and end-to-end density AL variants
topic_metadata.description: Wang et al. propose two variants of density-based active learning: one with fixed feature representations and another trained end-to-end. The fixed-representation variant resembles TypiClust but explicitly maximizes distances among selected samples to enhance diversity. The end-to-end variant jointly learns feature representations and sample selection using a learnable k-means clustering module, simultaneously optimizing cluster assignments and embeddings under a local smoothness constraint. This integrates representation learning and density-based selection into a unified training pipeline.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting with 'Wang et al. (2022c) proposed two variants of density-based AL.' through 'with a local smoothness constraint.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Computational trade-offs in AL methodologies
topic_metadata.description: Methodologically, cover-based AL involves solving an NP-hard problem and relies on greedy linear-time approximations whose distance from the optimal solution is unknown in practice. This makes it difficult to assess how much AL performance could improve with truly optimal coverage. Density-based AL replaces this NP-hard optimization with density estimation, which is generally more computationally efficient. Thus, density-based strategies offer a more tractable alternative while still guiding sample selection via inferred data distribution structure.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting with 'From the perspective of methodology,' through 'which is more computation-efficient.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Diversity sampling in deep active learning
topic_metadata.description: Diversity sampling aims to reduce redundancy among queried samples in active learning so that the annotation budget is not wasted on highly similar instances. By encouraging selection of less redundant data, it mitigates overfitting to a small, homogeneous training set and improves model performance. The section outlines four main diversity strategies: clustering, farthest-first traversal, determinantal point processes (DPPs), and methods tailored to specific informativeness metrics.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph of §3.3.1 (from “Diversity strategies aim to reduce sampling redundancy…” to “…tailored to certain informativeness metrics.”)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Random partitioning into stochastic batches
topic_metadata.description: Random selection is repurposed for diversity by partitioning the entire dataset into stochastic batches, which are then scored and selected based on batch-level uncertainty. In prostate and hippocampus segmentation tasks, the highest-uncertainty random batches were annotated, leading to consistent improvements of multiple uncertainty-based active learning methods under extremely low annotation budgets. This shows that simple random batch partitioning can act as an effective diversity mechanism when combined with uncertainty scoring.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting “Random Selection could also be used for better diversity…” through “…hippocampus segmentation.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Fisher information-based SDP diversity selection
topic_metadata.description: Fisher information (FI)-based active learning methods formulate batch selection as a semidefinite programming (SDP) problem that maximizes information gain while controlling redundancy. Different solvers and algorithms address the computational challenges of SDP: some work relies on off-the-shelf commercial solvers, while others introduce greedy algorithms tailored to high-dimensional feature spaces. These FI-SDP formulations provide a principled way to promote diversity grounded in information theory.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences “FI-based methods formulated AL as a semi-definite programming (SDP) problem…” through “…greedy algorithm to adapt to high-dimensional feature space.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Image hashing and locality-sensitive diversity
topic_metadata.description: Image hashing for diversity sampling compresses each image into a compact feature representation, such as its first principal component, and then uses locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) to bucket similar images together. Samples are drawn uniformly across buckets so that the labeled set spans many distinct regions of the feature space, reducing redundancy. Applied to skin lesion analysis, this method shows how simple hash-based partitioning can operationalize diversity in large-scale image pools.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final sentences starting “In skin lesion analysis, Shi et al. (2019) introduced image hashing for diversity sampling…” through the end of the section.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Long-Tail Class Distributions in Medical Tasks
topic_metadata.description: Many medical image classification problems exhibit a long-tail distribution, where a small number of classes are frequent and numerous rare classes have few examples. The section cites tasks such as skin lesion classification and whole-slide image classification as typical examples. These long-tail distributions complicate model learning because standard training objectives are dominated by common classes.
topic_metadata.text_span: middle of the section mentioning long tail distribution and example tasks

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Overfitting Majority and Underfitting Minority Classes
topic_metadata.description: Training deep learning models on imbalanced datasets tends to cause overfitting to majority classes and underfitting to minority classes. Majority classes are modeled very accurately but may not generalize well, while minority classes are poorly represented and lead to low sensitivity or recall. This imbalance in learning performance undermines the clinical reliability of medical image classifiers.
topic_metadata.text_span: sentences discussing training on imbalanced datasets and its effects

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Diversity sampling for imbalanced COVID-19
topic_metadata.description: In a class-imbalanced COVID-19 image classification dataset, multiple informativeness scores and sampling strategies were compared within an active learning framework. The findings indicated that diversity-based sampling, which prioritizes querying heterogeneous samples, is better suited than other strategies for mitigating class imbalance. This highlights diversity as a key selection criterion when majority and minority classes are unevenly represented.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences on Chong et al. (2021) at the beginning of the section ('In a class-imbalanced COVID-19 dataset, Chong et al. (2021)... diversity sampling is more favored for class-imbalance.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Tail-aware VAE–copula active sampling
topic_metadata.description: Jin et al. assumed that samples closer to the tail of the feature distribution are more likely to be from minority classes, equating tail probability with minority-class likelihood. They trained a variational autoencoder (VAE) for feature extraction and used copula models to estimate tail probabilities over these features, then combined clustering with unequal probability sampling to select informative samples. This tail-aware active learning approach was validated on the long-tailed ISIC 2020 skin lesion dataset.
topic_metadata.text_span: Middle of the classification paragraph describing Jin et al. (2022c) ('Jin et al. (2022c) assumed that samples closer to the tail... which has a long-tailed distribution.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Threshold-based minority class querying
topic_metadata.description: In blood cell detection under microscopy, Sadafi et al. designed an active learning rule that requests expert annotations when the predicted probability for the minority class exceeds a fixed threshold (0.2). This simple decision rule targets labeling efforts at cases likely to belong to the underrepresented class, improving class coverage without complex modeling. The strategy directly couples classifier confidence with annotation triggering.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence on Sadafi et al. (2019) ('In blood cell detection under microscopy, Sadafi et al. (2019)... exceeded 0.2.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Bayesian error decomposition for AL imbalance
topic_metadata.description: Choi et al. proposed estimating the probability that a classifier will make a mistake on a given sample and decomposing this error probability into three components via Bayes’ rule. They trained a VAE to model the likelihood of the data given a predicted class, and an auxiliary classifier on VAE features to estimate class priors and class-specific mislabeling probabilities. By jointly considering these three probabilities for query selection, they reduced class imbalance effects in active learning and showed good performance on stepwise class-imbalanced CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph segment beginning with 'Besides, Choi et al. (2021b)...' through 'datasets.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-based optimization for class balance
topic_metadata.description: Bengar et al. introduced an optimization-based active learning framework that explicitly maintains class balance while using uncertainty as a primary selection signal. When querying uncertain samples, the method compensates for underrepresented classes by adding the most confident samples from those minority classes to the query batch. This produces a more balanced labeled set over time, improving learning stability under class imbalance.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences on Bengar et al. (2022) ('For uncertainty-based methods, Bengar et al. (2022) introduced an optimization framework... in the queried dataset.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Class-balanced region sampling for segmentation
topic_metadata.description: In segmentation-focused active learning, some methods select regions or patches rather than full images, which risks missing rare or small structures such as the optic chiasma or optic nerve in head-and-neck multi-organ segmentation. To address this, Cai et al. and Wu et al. developed class-balanced region sampling strategies that bias region selection toward areas containing rare object classes. These strategies ensure that annotation effort covers critical but small anatomical structures within a region-querying AL setup.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final sentences under 'Segmentation:' discussing region-based selection and class-balanced strategies ('Segmentation: Due to certain AL methods selecting regions... as detailed in §4.3.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Hybrid sampling with multiple metrics
topic_metadata.description: Hybrid sampling in active learning addresses the challenge of effectively integrating multiple informativeness metrics when selecting unlabeled samples. Instead of relying on a single criterion, hybrid methods combine different notions such as uncertainty and representativeness to guide annotation. This aims to exploit complementary strengths of various metrics to improve label efficiency, especially in medical image analysis scenarios.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening paragraph of section 3.3.3 (first 5–6 sentences)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Multi-round sampling strategy
topic_metadata.description: Multi-round sampling sequentially applies different informativeness metrics, first filtering a subset of candidates by one metric and then refining selection within this subset using another. This staged strategy is popular in medical image analysis for its simplicity and flexibility, as demonstrated in several cited works. It enables a coarse-to-fine selection process where an initial metric narrows the pool and a secondary metric optimizes the final batch for annotation.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraph beginning 'Multi-round sampling first selects a subset...' up to 'for its convenience...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Combining representativeness and uncertainty
topic_metadata.description: Hybrid strategies often pair representativeness with uncertainty to balance coverage of the data distribution and model improvement. One example performs representativeness sampling conditioned on uncertainty scores to reduce redundancy in the selected set, ensuring diverse but informative samples. Another approach uses dynamic weights to allocate labeling budget between representativeness and uncertainty, prioritizing typical data early and uncertainty-focused refinement later as the model matures.
topic_metadata.text_span: sentences starting 'For example, SA (Yang et al., 2017)...' through '...by querying samples with erroneous predictions.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Metric fusion for hybrid sampling
topic_metadata.description: Metric fusion directly combines multiple informativeness scores into a single composite measure for sample selection. A simple instantiation is summing different metrics and querying samples with the highest aggregated values, enabling straightforward joint optimization of several criteria. This approach is widely adopted in medical-domain active learning, offering a more integrated alternative to sequential, multi-round strategies.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraph beginning 'Metrics fusion is another widely used approach...' through '...AL of the medical domain (Li et al., 2024; Zhou et al., 2021c; Wu et al., 2021).'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Ranked batch-mode adaptive metric fusion
topic_metadata.description: Ranked batch-mode active learning adaptively fuses multiple metrics when selecting batches of samples, rather than using fixed, predetermined combinations. It typically ranks unlabeled instances using several criteria and then integrates these rankings or scores to construct an optimal query batch. This adaptive fusion aims to better capture evolving informativeness patterns during the active learning process.
topic_metadata.text_span: final sentence: 'Besides, ranked batch-mode (Cardoso et al., 2017) can adaptively fuse multiple metrics in AL.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Reinforcement learning formulation of sample selection
topic_metadata.description: Sample selection is framed as a reinforcement learning problem where the learner and dataset form the environment, and the neural selector acts as the agent. The agent repeatedly chooses a limited number of samples for annotation and receives rewards that reflect the impact of these choices on downstream model performance. These rewards are used to train the neural selector’s policy, enabling adaptive, performance-driven sampling strategies.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraph beginning 'One of the most common methods of learnable sampling is to formulate sample selection as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Actor-critic neural selector for medical images
topic_metadata.description: An actor-critic framework is used where the actor implements the neural selector and the critic network evaluates the quality of selected samples. This setup learns to choose samples that most effectively improve medical image classification performance. The method is reported to perform excellently in lung CT disease classification and diabetic retinopathy classification from fundus images.
topic_metadata.text_span: sentences: 'In medical image classification, Wang et al. (2020b) employed an actor-critic framework...' through the performance comments on lung CT and diabetic retinopathy

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Probabilistic policy networks with REINFORCE
topic_metadata.description: A probabilistic policy network is employed as the neural selector, outputting distributions over samples to query. Rewards are designed to encourage selection of diverse and representative data points, aligning the sampling process with coverage of the data manifold. The policy is trained using the REINFORCE algorithm, a classic policy-gradient method for updating stochastic policies from reward signals.
topic_metadata.text_span: sentences: 'Besides, Haußmann et al. (2019) adopted a probabilistic policy network...' through 'The neural selector is trained using the REINFORCE algorithm (Williams, 1992).'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Few-shot and meta-learning neural selectors
topic_metadata.description: Beyond standard RL formulations, learnable sampling can also be cast as few-shot learning or approached via meta-learning to train neural selectors. These perspectives aim to learn sampling strategies that generalize across tasks or datasets, enabling rapid adaptation with limited labeled data. Such methods leverage prior experience to guide which samples are most beneficial to label in new scenarios.
topic_metadata.text_span: closing sentence: 'For more works on learnable sampling in AL, such as formulating AL as few-shot learning or training neural selectors by meta-learning, please refer to the survey of Liu et al. (2022).'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Leveraging idle unlabeled samples in AL cycles
topic_metadata.description: In standard active learning cycles, many unlabeled samples remain unused for training, effectively sitting idle while only queried samples are labeled and learned from. The text highlights this inefficiency and proposes combining active learning with semi-supervised learning so that both labeled and unlabeled images contribute to model training. This joint utilization can enhance data efficiency and model performance without increasing annotation demands. It reframes unlabeled pool data as a training asset rather than mere query candidates.
topic_metadata.text_span: sentences: 'However, massive unlabeled samples sit idle during the model training in the AL cycle. By combining the AL with semi-supervised learning, the model can be trained on both labeled and unlabeled samples.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty estimation with MC dropout
topic_metadata.description: Within the CEAL framework for melanoma segmentation, Monte Carlo (MC) dropout is used to estimate prediction uncertainty. By performing multiple stochastic forward passes with dropout enabled at test time, the method computes variability in predictions as an uncertainty measure. These uncertainty estimates guide which medical image samples are selected for expert annotation versus pseudo-labeling.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences describing Gorriz et al. (2017) and use of MC dropout (around 'Gorriz et al. (2017) adopted the CEAL framework...')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Refining pseudo-labels with dense CRFs
topic_metadata.description: In medical image segmentation, dense conditional random fields (CRFs) are applied to refine pseudo-labels generated by deep models. This post-processing step enforces spatial and appearance consistency across pixels, correcting local misclassifications in the initial pseudo-labels. Such refinement improves the quality of supervision when training segmentation networks with pseudo-labeled data.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence discussing Zhao et al. (2021) and dense conditional random fields (around 'Zhao et al. (2021) refined the pseudo-labels with dense conditional random fields.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Curriculum-based hard and easy sample selection
topic_metadata.description: For Gleason grading in prostate cancer histopathology, samples are categorized into hard and easy via curriculum learning. Hard samples, which are likely more informative or challenging, are always sent for oracle (expert) annotation. Easy samples are then further analyzed based on training behavior to decide whether they should be pseudo-labeled or discarded.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences on Li et al. (2022) and curriculum learning (around 'Li et al. (2022) proposed a new approach... They employed curriculum learning to categorize all samples into hard and easy.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Training loss for label-noise detection
topic_metadata.description: Training loss on easy samples is used as a proxy for label reliability in the pseudo-labeling process. Easy samples with low training loss are assumed to have reliable pseudo-labels and are included to assist training, whereas easy samples with high loss are treated as noisy and excluded. This mechanism adaptively filters pseudo-labeled data to reduce the impact of label noise in deep active learning for medical images.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final sentences detailing loss-based filtering of easy samples (around 'For the easy samples, they evaluated the presence of label noise based on the training loss...')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Integrating consistency-based SSL into AL
topic_metadata.description: Several works integrate semi-supervised learning methods that rely on consistency regularization into active learning pipelines for medical image analysis. Examples include combining MeanTeacher, VAT, and NoTeacher with AL for chest X-ray classification, and coupling a proposed COD method with MeanTeacher. Another line combines density-based active learning with multiple semi-supervised strategies, showing that such hybrids can outperform standard active learning and semi-supervised baselines.
topic_metadata.text_span: middle of section describing Balaram et al. (2022), Huang et al. (2021), and Wang et al. (2022c) (from 'Many works integrated existing consistency-based semi-supervised methods...' to '...excels in semi-supervised learning.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Consistency-based sample informativeness in AL
topic_metadata.description: Consistency is also used as a criterion to measure sample informativeness for active learning selection. In a semi-supervised AL framework, each unlabeled sample is passed through the model multiple times with random augmentations, and a consistency loss is defined by the variance between the multiple outputs. Samples exhibiting lower consistency (higher variance) are deemed more informative and are selected for annotation. This joint use of consistency for both semi-supervised training and query strategy leads to significant performance gains.
topic_metadata.text_span: later middle of section describing Gao et al. (2020) (from 'Consistency could be also used for sample selection.' to 'Results showed that combining AL with semi-supervised learning significantly improves performance.')

Table 2: Methodology summarization of surveyed active learning works.
topic_metadata.title: Single vs multiple inference strategies
topic_metadata.description: The methodologies are categorized into single-model inference and multiple-inference schemes for estimating uncertainty. Single-model methods rely on one deterministic pass to compute measures like distance to the decision boundary, while multiple-inference strategies (e.g., MC Dropout or data disagreement across inferences) approximate distributions over predictions. This distinction reflects different ways to capture epistemic uncertainty in deep active learning.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Single-model uncertainty sampling strategies
topic_metadata.description: This topic covers deep active learning that relies on a single predictive model and classical uncertainty-based query strategies. Acquisition functions such as Least Confidence, Margin, and Entropy are used to score unlabeled samples, often selecting the Top-k highest-uncertainty instances for annotation. Pseudo-labeling may be applied to leverage model predictions on unlabeled data, integrating semi-supervised learning with active selection.

topic_metadata.title: Ensemble-based multi-criterion acquisition functions
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes ensemble-based deep active learning that evaluates unlabeled data using multiple acquisition criteria simultaneously. Metrics such as Entropy, BALD (Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreement), Least Confidence, and Variance are computed from ensemble predictions to capture different facets of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. Samples are then ranked and the Top-k most informative instances are selected at each iteration.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Entropy, Least Confidence, and Variance Measures
topic_metadata.description: Uncertainty sampling in deep active learning commonly employs prediction entropy, least confidence, or variance to rank unlabeled samples. Entropy and least confidence operate on the output probability distribution, while variance is often derived from multiple inferences to capture prediction instability. Within each cluster, it selects samples with maximum information density, aiming to capture representative and informative points. BIRCH is chosen over k-Means because it is less sensitive to outliers and can better identify noisy samples, improving robustness of the initial labeled set. topic_metadata.title: Contrastive-loss based cold-start AL
topic_metadata.description: Chen et al. (2023b) use the loss from momentum contrastive learning to address the cold-start problem in active learning for medical image analysis. They assume that higher contrastive losses indicate samples more representative of the underlying data distribution. Unlabeled data are clustered with k-Means, and within each cluster the samples with the highest contrastive loss are selected for annotation, which helps mitigate class imbalance and improve anomaly detection when few labeled samples are available. The approach is validated on PathMNIST, OrganMNIST, and BloodMNIST datasets.

topic_metadata.title: Redundancy in Full-Image Annotation
topic_metadata.description: In fine-grained medical imaging tasks like segmentation and detection, labeling entire images can be redundant and waste annotation budget. Large, easily segmented organs (e.g., liver, spleen) do not require dense labeling to improve model performance. In contrast, small, hard-to-segment organs such as the esophagus and adrenal glands would benefit more from focused annotation. This highlights the mismatch between uniform full-image labeling and the heterogeneous difficulty across anatomical structures.

topic_metadata.title: Spatial Confidence Aggregation over Patches

Each slide is split into patches, per-patch confidence (e.g., maximum predictive probability) is computed, and a 5×5 mean filter aggregates neighboring confidences into a regional metric. Regions corresponding to low aggregated confidence (high uncertainty) are then prioritized for annotation, capturing spatial context rather than treating patches independently.

topic_metadata.description: Chen et al. (2021) trained a bidirectional GAN to learn the underlying data manifold and corresponding latent/feature representations. This method combines generative modeling with uncertainty estimation to drive targeted sample synthesis in deep active learning.

topic_metadata.title: Physics-based simulation for labeling synthetics
topic_metadata.description: To avoid reliance on experts for labeling low-quality or numerous synthetic images, Chen et al. used physics-based simulation to generate labels for the GAN-produced samples. topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Domain Adaptation: Tackling Distribution Shift
topic_metadata.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation and Performance Gap
topic_metadata.description: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) is a dominant DA setting where the source domain is labeled and the target domain is entirely unlabeled. While UDA can yield strong performance on the target domain, it typically still underperforms compared to fully supervised learning directly on the target domain. This performance gap motivates strategies that incorporate some level of target-domain annotation.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Domain Adaptation: Tackling Distribution Shift
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty, Representativeness, and Domainness in ADA
topic_metadata.description: In ADA, query strategies must balance uncertainty (how unsure the model is about predictions) and representativeness (how well a sample reflects the target domain distribution). Representativeness in this context is often termed domainness or targetness, capturing how strongly a sample belongs to the target domain. These criteria jointly guide which target samples should be annotated to most effectively improve cross-domain performance.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences discussing query criteria in ADA ('For better queries in ADA, one should consider both uncertainty and representativeness... referred to as domainness or targetness').

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Adversarial learning with importance sampling
topic_metadata.description: Su et al. (2020) introduce ADA by combining domain adversarial learning with active learning through importance sampling. A domain discriminator and a task model jointly estimate which target samples are both uncertain for the task and highly different from the source domain. These samples are then prioritized for annotation to simultaneously improve task performance and reduce domain discrepancy.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Domainness-aware committee and filtering strategy
topic_metadata.description: Fu et al. (2021) integrate query-by-committee, uncertainty, and domainness into an ADA framework. A domain discriminator scores target samples by domainness, while Gaussian kernels filter out anomalous and source-similar target samples to avoid outliers and redundant data. Random sampling is additionally used to enhance diversity among selected images, balancing informativeness and coverage.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-weighted clustering of target images
topic_metadata.description: Prabhu et al. (2021) apply k-means clustering on target-domain samples and select cluster centers as candidates for annotation. These centers are weighted by predictive uncertainty, so that clusters with more uncertain samples contribute more to the selection. This ensures that chosen images are both diverse in feature space and highly informative for the model.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Anchor-based selection for segmentation ADA
topic_metadata.description: For segmentation tasks, Ning et al. (2021) introduce anchors built from source-domain class-wise feature concatenations whose cluster centers act as reference anchors. Distances are computed between each target sample and its nearest anchor in this feature space. Target images with the largest distances—indicating poor alignment with source anchors—are queried for annotation to better cover underrepresented or shifted regions.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Energy-based image selection in ADA
topic_metadata.description: Xie et al. (2022b) adapt the concept of energy, defined as inversely proportional to data likelihood, for ADA. A model trained on the source domain computes energy scores for target-domain samples, with high-energy samples corresponding to low-likelihood, out-of-distribution or shifted data. By selecting high-energy images for annotation, the method targets samples that are representative of the target domain yet substantially different from the source.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Prototype inconsistency and uncertainty-based querying
topic_metadata.description: Huang et al. (2023) propose selecting target samples that exhibit both high prediction uncertainty and inconsistency with their nearest prototypes. Prototypes summarize class-wise or feature-wise typical patterns, and inconsistency indicates a sample that deviates from these learned norms. This dual criterion aims to capture samples that are both hard for the model and atypical relative to established representations.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Dual-reference strategy for tumor segmentation ADA
topic_metadata.description: In nasopharyngeal carcinoma tumor segmentation, Wang et al. (2023) propose a dual-reference strategy using both source- and target-domain cues. Source-domain feature representations are clustered to form reference samples, and target images with the highest and lowest similarity to these references are selected. These extremes are interpreted as domain-invariant (high similarity) and domain-specific (low similarity) samples, respectively, jointly improving generalization and adaptation.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: LabOR: disagreement-based region selection
topic_metadata.description: LabOR uses an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) pre-trained model to generate pseudo-labels for target-domain samples and trains two segmentation heads on these labels. It then maximizes prediction disagreement between the two heads and queries annotations for regions exhibiting the highest disagreement, treating disagreement as an informativeness measure. This strategy enables LabOR to achieve performance close to full supervision while annotating only 2.2% of target-domain regions.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty and regional impurity for patch querying
topic_metadata.description: This approach selects the most informative patches based on a combination of prediction uncertainty and regional impurity. Regional impurity is defined as the number of unique predicted classes within a pixel’s neighborhood, capturing edge or boundary complexity, which often indicates challenging regions. By querying extremely small patches (e.g., 3×3) with high uncertainty and impurity, the method attains near fully supervised performance with only about 5% of the annotation cost.

topic_metadata.title: Density-based superpixel selection with GMMs
topic_metadata.description: This method models the distribution of superpixels in both source and target domains using Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) as density estimators. It then selects superpixels in the target domain that have high density under the target GMM but low density under the source GMM, identifying representative yet domain-specific regions for annotation. The density-based criterion aims to focus labeling effort on characteristic target structures that are underrepresented or mismatched in the source domain.

topic_metadata.title: Saliency-map aggregation for sample selection
topic_metadata.description: Mahapatra et al. (2021) proposed using saliency maps to identify informative chest X-ray samples for annotation in an active learning loop. Per-pixel saliency maps are aggregated into a single scalar score per image, using three strategies: kurtosis of the saliency distribution, multivariate radiomic features, and deep features derived from autoencoders combined with clustering. Comparative results showed that aggregation based on deep autoencoder features yields the most effective selection of informative samples.

topic_metadata.title: Boundary-based AL with entropy and pseudo-labels
topic_metadata.description: Nguyen et al. Their strategy sends high-entropy (high-uncertainty) samples to experts for labeling, while assigning pseudo-labels to confident samples to expand training data without manual effort. Momentum updates are incorporated to stabilize predictions over time, reducing fluctuations in sample selection and improving the robustness of the active learning process.

topic_metadata.title: Entropy-based uncertainty with pseudo-labeling
topic_metadata.description: In breast pathology image classification, active learning is implemented by measuring entropy over model predictions on patches to quantify uncertainty. Patches with high entropy are sent to experts for annotation, while low-entropy patches receive pseudo-labels and are used to augment the training set without manual labeling. This combines uncertainty sampling with semi-supervised learning to improve annotation efficiency. The key entities are patch-level predictions, entropy as an uncertainty metric, and pseudo-label assignment.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Pathological Whole-slide Images and Multiple Instance
topic_metadata.title: Category-wise curriculum querying and negative pre-training
topic_metadata.description: For histological tissue classification at the patch level, category-wise curriculum querying dynamically adjusts how much uncertainty sampling focuses on each class. This addresses class-dependent difficulty and imbalance by weighting querying effort per category during active learning. Additionally, negative pre-training uses intentionally wrong predictions to better separate visually similar classes, improving discriminative representations before or during active learning. Together, these strategies refine query selection and representation learning in complex multi-class pathology settings.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Pathological Whole-slide Images and Multiple Instance
topic_metadata.title: Human-augmenting AI labeling with Core-Set AL
topic_metadata.description: A human-augmenting labeling system leverages active learning to suggest which WSI patches experts should annotate and to propose labels via a trained classifier. Core-Set is used as the active learner to select a subset of patches that best represent the data distribution while being informative. This human-in-the-loop workflow significantly reduces pathologists’ workload (around 90%) and can slightly improve data quality across cellular labeling tasks. The process couples query selection, model training, and expert verification in an iterative loop.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Pathological Whole-slide Images and Multiple Instance
topic_metadata.title: Attention-based MIL with MC Dropout for querying
topic_metadata.description: In MIL-based WSI classification, attention-based MIL architectures are combined with Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout to estimate uncertainty at both the attention (instance importance) and classification levels. For each patch within a WSI, MC Dropout yields predictive distributions from which uncertainties are computed, and patches with the highest uncertainties are selected for expert annotation. This dual uncertainty captures ambiguity in which patches matter and how they should be classified, improving the informativeness of queried instances. The method aligns instance-level querying with the MIL attention mechanism.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Pathological Whole-slide Images and Multiple Instance
topic_metadata.title: Open-set active learning for relevant patch selection
topic_metadata.description: Because WSIs contain both target classes (e.g., tumors, lymph nodes, normal cells) and many irrelevant non-target tissues (e.g., fat, stroma, debris), open-set active learning is adopted. In this setting, the unlabeled pool includes both target and non-target samples, and the system must simultaneously perform relevance filtering and uncertainty-based querying. By combining feature distribution information with prediction uncertainty, the method selects patches that are both informative and likely to belong to target classes for annotation. This reduces annotation spent on clearly irrelevant or out-of-distribution regions while focusing expert effort on diagnostically meaningful instances.

topic_metadata.title: Hybrid uncertainty-representativeness for slice annotation
topic_metadata.description: Recent methods for slice-based annotation combine uncertainty with representativeness to select informative samples. In shoulder MRI musculoskeletal segmentation, Ozdemir et al. (2021) measure uncertainty using the variance across multiple Monte Carlo (MC) dropout runs and measure representativeness using posterior probabilities estimated by an infoVAE. This balances querying slices where the model is unsure with slices that are representative of the data distribution. Such hybrid criteria aim to improve both sample informativeness and coverage of the feature space.

topic_metadata.title: Bayesian U-net and MI-based redundancy reduction
topic_metadata.description: Li et al. (2024) propose a hybrid deep active learning strategy for musculoskeletal segmentation of lower extremities in MRI and CT. Uncertainty is estimated using a Bayesian U-net, while representativeness is computed via cosine similarity, ensuring both informative and diverse slice selection. They additionally apply mutual information-based criteria to minimize sample redundancy, following Nath et al. (2021), further improving the efficiency of queried samples. This integrated approach achieves strong performance across both MRI and CT datasets.

topic_metadata.title: Self-supervised features for one-shot sampling
topic_metadata.description: Most one-shot annotation methods in medical imaging combine self-supervised feature learning with tailored sampling strategies. Self-supervised representations (e.g., from VAEs, contrastive learning, or auto-encoding transformations) capture semantic structure without extensive labels, enabling more informed selection of samples within a single round. These learned features then drive criteria like representativeness, diversity, or density for sample selection.

topic_metadata.description: The RA method is an early one-shot active learning approach for medical image segmentation that leverages features from a variational autoencoder (VAE). It uses a representativeness strategy in the learned feature space to select informative samples for single-round annotation. RA showed strong performance on gland segmentation in pathological images, whole-heart MRI segmentation, and fungal segmentation in electron microscopic images.

topic_metadata.title: Representativeness-based key slice selection
topic_metadata.description: Wu et al. proposed a representativeness-based framework focused on selecting key slices for annotation in a one-shot setting. They employ self-learning to obtain semantic representations for each slice, then use these features to propagate expert annotations to unannotated slices. This approach reduces the number of slices needing direct expert labeling while maintaining segmentation quality across the volume.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Contrastive features and farthest-first sampling
topic_metadata.description: Jin et al. (2022b) integrate contrastive learning features with a farthest-first sampling strategy to realize one-shot annotation. Contrastive learning yields discriminative embeddings, while farthest-first sampling selects samples that are maximally separated in this feature space, promoting diversity and broad coverage. Their method was validated on ISIC 2018 skin lesion and lung segmentation datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness for single-round labeling.

topic_metadata.title: Density-based selection via reachable distance
topic_metadata.description: Jin et al. (2023b) use auto-encoding transformations for self-supervised feature learning, capturing meaningful structure in unlabeled medical images. In the resulting feature space, they define a notion of reachable distance to estimate local sample density and select high-density samples for annotation in one shot. This favors labeling representative points in dense regions, which can improve generalization while respecting strict interaction limits.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Unequal annotation costs in segmentation
topic_metadata.description: The section highlights that common active learning methods assume equal annotation costs per sample, which is unrealistic in medical image segmentation where annotation time can vary significantly. It argues that active learning should explicitly consider annotation costs, such as annotation time, to better support physicians and make querying more practical in clinical settings.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Disagreement-time cost model with knapsack AL
topic_metadata.description: Kuo et al. (2018) integrate predictive disagreement and estimated annotation time to guide sample selection for intracranial hemorrhage detection in CT scans. Jensen–Shannon divergence between multiple model outputs measures informativeness, while annotation time is approximated using the segmentation boundary length and number of connected components. The selection problem is formulated as a 0–1 knapsack optimization, solved via dynamic programming, to choose the most informative samples under a cost budget.

topic_metadata.title: Similarity-based slice annotation cost
topic_metadata.description: Shen et al. (2021) estimate the annotation cost of brain tumor slices using a distance measure between queried slices and already-labeled slices. Lower distance is interpreted as lower annotation cost, under the assumption that annotating slices similar to previously labeled ones is faster and easier for experts. This embeds a notion of familiarity into the active learning cost model.

topic_metadata.description: Atzeni et al. (2022) refine annotation cost estimation for brain structure segmentation by accounting for spatial relationships between multiple regions of interest. They also use the average Dice coefficient from previous active learning rounds to predict current Dice performance. Regions are then selected for annotation to maximize the predicted average Dice, linking cost modeling with an explicit segmentation quality metric.

topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-Guided Interactive Fetal Brain Segmentation
topic_metadata.description: For MRI fetal brain segmentation, an uncertainty-guided interactive refinement framework is introduced. A specialized network architecture produces multiple segmentation outputs simultaneously; the variance across these predictions is used as an uncertainty metric. Slices with the highest estimated uncertainty are prioritized for human expert interaction, allowing clinicians to focus refinement on the most ambiguous regions, thereby improving segmentation quality with minimal additional annotation.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Learning for Medical Image Reconstruction
topic_metadata.title: Learnable k-space sampling for MRI
topic_metadata.description: Deep learning is used to reconstruct undersampled MRI data where k-space is sampled via either fixed or learnable masks. Traditional approaches use a fixed undersampling mask and a deep model to reconstruct the image, while AL-based approaches learn which k-space locations to sample next. This transforms acquisition into an adaptive sampling problem directly tied to reconstruction quality and imaging speed.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Learning for Medical Image Reconstruction
topic_metadata.title: Adversarial and RL policies for k-space
topic_metadata.description: Adversarial learning and reinforcement learning are used to design active sampling policies in k-space for MRI. Methods include an adversarially trained evaluator that selects the next k-space row, dual deep Q-networks for active sampling decisions, and policy-gradient-based networks that adapt sampling patterns. Rewards are defined via reconstruction metrics such as structural similarity, linking sampling choices to image quality improvements.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Learning for Medical Image Reconstruction
topic_metadata.title: Joint optimization of acquisition and reconstruction
topic_metadata.description: Instead of treating acquisition and reconstruction separately, some MRI approaches jointly optimize the sampling policy and the reconstruction network. This end-to-end training allows the acquisition strategy to adapt to the reconstruction model’s capabilities, potentially yielding better image quality for a given acquisition budget. It exemplifies tightly coupled AL and reconstruction design.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Learning for Medical Image Reconstruction
topic_metadata.title: Adaptive CT scanning angle selection
topic_metadata.description: Active learning is applied to CT by adaptively choosing patient-specific scanning angles. The method tailors the projection directions to each individual, enabling sufficient reconstruction quality with fewer projections. This reduces both radiation exposure and scan duration compared to fixed-angle protocols.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Active Learning for Medical Image Reconstruction
topic_metadata.title: Active rescanning in electron microscopy
topic_metadata.description: In electron microscopy, an AL pipeline first enhances low-resolution images to high resolution, then predicts regions of interest and reconstruction errors. A weighted determinantal point process (DPP), parameterized by reconstruction error, selects which pixels to rescan to refine the image. This strategy simultaneously maintains low reconstruction error and spatial diversity, focusing acquisition on informative and diverse locations.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Performance Evaluation of Active Learning in Medical
topic_metadata.title: Limitations of Existing AL Evaluations
topic_metadata.description: Active learning (AL) for medical image analysis lacks comprehensive and systematic evaluation on realistic medical datasets. Many studies rely on standard benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, or MedMNIST, which do not fully capture the limited data availability and higher complexity of real-world clinical imaging. This mismatch raises concerns about the clinical applicability of reported performance gains.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Performance Evaluation of Active Learning in Medical
topic_metadata.title: Inconsistent Gains Over Random Sampling
topic_metadata.description: Different AL strategies often exhibit inconsistent performance and do not reliably outperform simple random sampling, especially in classification tasks. Studies, including Munjal et al. (2022) and prior discussion in §4.2, report that no single AL method consistently dominates others and that random sampling can be competitive or even superior when the annotation budget is low. This uncertainty makes it difficult to decide which AL method to adopt for a given medical imaging scenario.

topic_metadata.description: This topic addresses the use of deep active learning in electron microscopy (EM) for brain imaging, including mouse cortex (SNEMI3D) and human cerebrum data. Methods target accelerated acquisition and analysis of EM volumes by prioritizing which regions or samples to acquire at high resolution and to annotate, thus reducing the immense labeling burden typical of EM datasets. The work referenced (Pineda et al. 2020, MICCAI) explores strategies to efficiently reconstruct or segment neural structures from large-scale EM imagery.

topic_metadata.description: Accuracy (ACC) is used as the primary evaluation metric for the multi-class classification task on the NCT-CRC-HE-100K dataset. It measures the proportion of correctly classified samples over the total number of samples, providing a straightforward indicator of overall classification performance. This choice is suitable when class distributions are relatively balanced and all classes are equally important.

topic_metadata.title: Test-Set Metrics as Final Results
topic_metadata.description: Evaluation metrics are ultimately computed on the testing set and reported as the final results. topic_metadata.title: Random sampling baseline in AL
topic_metadata.description: Random sampling is used as the baseline comparison method in the active learning (AL) evaluation. It selects unlabeled samples uniformly at random without using any model-driven informativeness or diversity criteria. This provides a reference to measure the benefit of more sophisticated query strategies.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Classic uncertainty-based AL criteria
topic_metadata.description: Confidence, Entropy, and Margin are presented as classic uncertainty-based active learning methods. They compute uncertainty scores from prediction probabilities using three different measures: low maximum confidence, high entropy, and small classification margin indicate greater uncertainty. These scores guide the selection of unlabeled samples expected to most improve the model when labeled.

Lower confidence, higher entropy, and lower margin indicate higher uncertainty.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: k-Center-Greedy for core-set selection
topic_metadata.description: k-Center-Greedy is used as the selection algorithm to balance computational cost and active learning performance. At each step, it greedily selects the point that maximizes the minimum distance to already selected points, approximating the k-center objective in embedding space. This yields a diverse and representative labeled set without the cost of exact optimization.
