topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty aggregation in segmentation tasks
topic_metadata.description: For segmentation, uncertainty-based methods differ from classification by operating initially at the pixel level. Pixel-wise scores (e.g., probabilities or uncertainty measures per pixel) are first produced, and then aggregated by averaging across pixels to obtain a single uncertainty score per image or sample. This aggregated score is then used for sample selection in active learning.

Specifically, we first produced the pixel-wise scores and then utilized the averaged scores for sample selection in the segmentation task.'

topic_metadata.title: Classification backbone and training setup
topic_metadata.description: The classification tasks use ResNet-18 as the backbone network, optimized with stochastic gradient descent with momentum. Training runs for 100 epochs with a batch size of 128, a learning rate of 0.01, momentum of 0.9, and cross-entropy as the loss function. A cosine learning rate decay schedule is applied to achieve smoother convergence during optimization.

(2018) is followed, including random cropping, flipping, rotation, affine transforms, and color jittering, to model more complex variability in dermoscopic images.

topic_metadata.title: U-Net segmentation architecture design
topic_metadata.description: Segmentation tasks are handled using a 5-level U-Net architecture, with symmetric encoder and decoder paths. Each level contains two blocks, and each block is composed of a 2D convolution, a dropout layer with probability 0.1, batch normalization, and a leaky ReLU activation. This configuration balances regularization, stable training, and non-linear feature extraction for pixel-wise prediction.

topic_metadata.title: Margin sampling in low-budget regimes
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes the behavior of the Margin-based active learning strategy when only a small labeling budget is available. Margin performs well in this regime because it leverages information from wrong predictions between similar classes to select informative samples. This aligns with findings reported in related work (Hu et al. 2023), highlighting the value of uncertainty near decision boundaries for early-stage labeling.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Effectiveness on Different Distances between Images
topic_metadata.title: L2 and cosine distances on embeddings
topic_metadata.description: This topic defines how L2 and cosine distances are computed over feature embeddings of images in deep active learning. Each image sample x is mapped to a d-dimensional feature vector z, and the L2 distance is calculated as the Euclidean norm of the difference between two embeddings, while the cosine distance is derived from one minus the cosine similarity between them. These formulas formalize how image similarity is quantified in the feature space for AL methods.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Effectiveness on Different Distances between Images
topic_metadata.title: Budget-dependent metric performance on datasets
topic_metadata.description: This topic summarizes empirical results comparing L2 and cosine distances across multiple medical imaging datasets and labeling budgets. On NCT-CRC-HE-100K, both metrics perform similarly at all budgets, whereas on ISIC 2020 and ACDC, L2 is better in early rounds (low budget) but cosine becomes competitive or superior as more samples are selected (high budget). The findings lead to a recommendation that L2 is generally preferable for low-budget scenarios, while cosine distance may be more advantageous when the annotation budget is high and the model is more mature.

topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Better Uncertainty
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty as a driver in AL
topic_metadata.description: Uncertainty is emphasized as a central signal in active learning, guiding which samples should be queried for annotation. The section suggests that current uncertainty estimates can be improved so that they more directly correspond to where the model is likely to be wrong, instead of merely being numerically high. This reframing positions uncertainty as a tool to expose model weaknesses rather than a generic confidence score.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening sentences: 'In AL, uncertainty plays a pivotal role. However, it would be beneficial if the uncertainty more directly highlighted the model’s mistakes.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Better Uncertainty
topic_metadata.title: Querying samples with inaccurate predictions
topic_metadata.description: The text proposes that active learning performance can be enhanced by preferentially querying samples on which the model currently makes incorrect predictions. This contrasts with querying solely based on high uncertainty and implies a tighter coupling between error detection and query strategy. The idea is that an ideal uncertainty measure should correlate strongly with prediction inaccuracy, making error-prone samples more likely to be selected.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening paragraph: 'We can enhance the model’s performance by querying samples with inaccurate predictions.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Learnable performance estimation for QC
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes learnable performance estimation methods for automated quality control (QC) of deep model outputs in medical image analysis. Examples include the Segment Anything Model (SAM) providing IoU estimates per mask, deep generative models predicting Dice scores for cardiac MRI segmentation, and auxiliary networks predicting Dice for brain tissue segmentation. These approaches estimate segmentation quality directly and are proposed as promising tools to support uncertainty-based active learning and mitigate model over-confidence.
topic_metadata.text_span: Middle of the section starting from "Recently, many works have adopted learnable performance estimation for quality control..." through "Hence, delving deeper into their potential for uncertainty-based AL is crucial to effectively tackle the issue of over-confidence."

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Probability calibration for uncertainty-based AL
topic_metadata.description: This topic covers probability calibration as a means to address over-confidence in deep models used for uncertainty-based active learning. Calibration measures the alignment between predicted probabilities and true outcomes, with over-confident models being poorly calibrated; examples include polyp classifiers where confidence should match actual polyp prevalence. The text discusses that ensembles can be better calibrated than MC Dropout, and Dirichlet-based methods consider all prediction outcomes, but most approaches only propose improved uncertainty metrics and perform post-hoc calibration. Existing calibration methods often require additional labeled datasets, highlighting the open problem of integrating calibration directly into uncertainty-based active learning pipelines.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting from "Moreover, improving the probability calibration of model prediction..." through "Therefore, integrating probability calibration into uncertainty-based AL represents a valuable research direction worth exploring."

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Better Generative Models
topic_metadata.title: Diffusion models with superior generative quality
topic_metadata.description: Diffusion models are highlighted as a newer class of generative models achieving state-of-the-art image quality. They iteratively denoise random noise into coherent images, and recent work (Kazerouni et al., 2023) demonstrates that they can surpass GANs on standard generative benchmarks. This improved fidelity and diversity make them attractive candidates for data generation within active learning frameworks.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence: 'Recently, diffusion models (Kazerouni et al., 2023) have advanced in achieving state-of-the-art generative quality.'

topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Better Generative Models
topic_metadata.title: Text-to-image diffusion for flexible generation
topic_metadata.description: Text-to-image diffusion models, exemplified by Stable Diffusion, are described as revolutionizing image generation by conditioning on natural language prompts. Their high-quality, text-guided outputs enable users to specify semantic content and appearance details directly through text. This controllability can support more targeted synthesis of rare or informative cases for active learning in medical imaging contexts.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Better Generative Models
topic_metadata.title: ControlNet for structure-conditioned diffusion
topic_metadata.description: ControlNet is introduced as an extension that allows diffusion models to follow detailed structural conditions, such as sketches or segmentation masks. By injecting additional control signals, it preserves global semantics from text while aligning local structures to given guidance maps. This mechanism can generate anatomically consistent or label-aligned images that are valuable for annotation-efficient learning and structured data augmentation.

topic_metadata.title: Integrating diffusion models into deep AL
topic_metadata.description: The section emphasizes that systematically exploring diffusion models within deep active learning remains an open research direction. Potential integrations include using diffusion-based generators to propose informative queries, synthesize hard or underrepresented cases, or model uncertainty in the data space. The authors position this as a promising avenue to surpass current GAN-centric AL strategies, especially in medical image analysis.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.section_heading: Towards Active Learning with Foundation Models
topic_metadata.title: Foundation models in active learning
topic_metadata.description: The section highlights how visual foundation models such as CLIP, SAM, and large language models like GPT-4 are shifting paradigms in medical image analysis and computer vision. These models, rich in prior knowledge, open new opportunities to redesign and improve active learning (AL) pipelines by leveraging their generalizable representations. The focus is on how this new class of models changes the context in which AL is developed and applied.

topic_metadata.title: Core methods in deep active learning
topic_metadata.description: The survey is described as comprehensively reviewing core methodological approaches in deep active learning. This implies coverage of key query strategies, model architectures, and selection criteria that underpin how deep active learning systems are designed and evaluated. These core methods form the technical foundation upon which more specialized and application-specific techniques are built.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comprehensive survey on deep active learning and its applications in medical image analysis
topic_metadata.title: Active learning tailored to medical imaging
topic_metadata.description: The survey specifically focuses on active learning methods that are customized for medical image analysis tasks. Such tailoring can involve adapting query strategies, model designs, or annotation interfaces to the unique properties of medical images (e.g., 3D volumes, multi-modal data) and clinical labels. The conclusion underscores the importance of domain-specific adaptations rather than generic active learning pipelines.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Challenges adapting classical AL to deep learning
topic_metadata.description: When transferring traditional active learning methods to deep learning, feature representations become dynamically learned and evolve during training, making pre-computation of pairwise distances or similarities for representativeness-based measures infeasible. Additionally, DNNs tend to be over-confident in their predictions, which can undermine uncertainty estimation for unlabeled samples. Although prior work has comprehensively summarized DAL methods, a lack of cross-dataset, cross-task experimental comparisons makes it difficult to know which DAL algorithms suit which tasks.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph of section 1 (from 'DAL originated from AL for classical ML tasks...' to 'Our work aims to fill this gap.')

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: DeepAL+ benchmarking toolkit for DAL
topic_metadata.description: DeepAL+ is a DAL benchmark toolkit that re-implements 19 DAL methods, extending a previous toolkit (DeepAL) that contained 11 highly-cited approaches before 2018. It upgrades prior implementations, adds more recent and highly-cited DAL algorithms, and expands the range of tasks and datasets to include standard image benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR, SVHN), medical image analysis, and object recognition with spurious correlations. Using DeepAL+, the authors conduct comparative experiments across multiple tasks, analyzing factors such as batch size, number of training epochs per AL iteration, and timing costs. The toolkit is designed to be extensible, enabling easy integration of new tasks, datasets, DAL algorithms, and base models, and is publicly released on GitHub.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Gradient-based active learning criteria
topic_metadata.description: Gradient-utilizing strategies estimate the impact of labeling a sample by examining gradients of the loss with respect to model parameters. They approximate how much the model would change if a candidate point were labeled and used for training, often via gradient norms or influence scores. This aligns selection with expected parameter updates rather than just prediction scores. Such methods are particularly suited to deep networks where gradients carry rich sensitivity information.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Representative diversity-based DAL strategies
topic_metadata.description: Representative/diversity-based deep active learning (DAL) aims to select samples that are diverse and representative of the unlabeled pool. The section lists three main mechanisms: clustering, discriminative learning, and point processes. Concrete example methods include K-means-based selection, the Corset approach, Cluster-Margin, DAL, VAAL, WAAL, BADGE (DPPS version), and Active DPP, each operationalizing diversity or representativeness differently.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-based deep active learning
topic_metadata.description: Uncertainty-based DAL selects unlabeled samples exhibiting high uncertainty, explicitly distinguishing aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Aleatoric uncertainty stems from inherent randomness in data generation processes, while epistemic uncertainty arises from limited model knowledge and can be reduced with more data. The text notes that many such DAL measures are adapted from pool-based active learning techniques developed for classical machine learning tasks, and that these methods form a standard family of querying strategies.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Maximum Entropy (Entropy) [61] selects data x that maximize the predictive entropy HM[y|x]:
topic_metadata.title: Predictive entropy over posterior probabilities
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes the mathematical formulation of predictive entropy HM[y|x] as −∑_k p_M(y = k | x) log p_M(y = k | x). The entropy is computed over the posterior label probabilities p_M(y | x) given by the classifier M for each class k. It quantifies the uncertainty of the model’s prediction for a given input by measuring how spread out the probability mass is across classes.
topic_metadata.text_span: Formula segment: 'αentropy(x, M) = HM[y|x] = −∑_k pM(y = k|x) log pM(y = k|x), where pM(y|x) is the posterior label probability from the classifier M.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Least Conﬁdence (LeastConf) [69] selects data x whose most likely label ˆy has lowest posterior
topic_metadata.title: Least Confidence active learning heuristic
topic_metadata.description: Least Confidence (LeastConf) is an uncertainty-based query strategy that selects data points x for which the model M has the lowest posterior probability on its most likely predicted label ŷ. The acquisition function is defined as α_LeastConf(x, M) = − p_M(ŷ | x), so higher acquisition scores correspond to lower model confidence. This method focuses solely on the top predicted class probability as a proxy for uncertainty, without considering the full predictive distribution over labels.
topic_metadata.text_span: Opening sentence and formula defining αLeastConf(x, M) = −pM(ŷ|x)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Least Conﬁdence (LeastConf) [69] selects data x whose most likely label ˆy has lowest posterior
topic_metadata.title: Variation Ratios as lack-of-confidence measure
topic_metadata.description: Variation Ratios (VarRatio) is presented as a method similar to Least Confidence that also targets the model's lack of confidence in its predictions. Its acquisition function is α_VarRatio(x, M) = 1 − p_M(ŷ | x), which measures how far the top predicted class probability is from full certainty. Like LeastConf, it relies on the most likely label’s posterior probability but expresses uncertainty as a complement (1 minus that probability).
topic_metadata.text_span: Second sentence describing VarRatio and its formula αVarRatio(x, M) = 1 − pM(ŷ|x)

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreements (BALD) [20, 26] chooses data points that are
topic_metadata.title: Mutual information-based acquisition function
topic_metadata.description: The BALD score is defined as the mutual information between the model’s predictions y and the posterior distribution over parameters p(ω|D_l). This is expressed as the difference between the predictive entropy H_M[y|x] and the expected conditional entropy E_{p(ω|D_l)}[H_M[y|x, ω]]. The first term measures overall predictive uncertainty, while the second term averages uncertainty conditioned on specific parameter settings, isolating epistemic uncertainty due to parameter uncertainty. This decomposition is central to how BALD quantifies and selects informative data points.
topic_metadata.text_span: Formula and explanation: '...mutual information between predictions and model posterior: αBALD(x, M) = HM[y|x] − Ep(ω|Dl)[HM[y|x, ω]]'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Mean Standard Deviation (MeanSTD) [29] maximizes the mean standard deviation of the pre-
topic_metadata.title: Mean Standard Deviation uncertainty measure
topic_metadata.description: Mean Standard Deviation (MeanSTD) is an acquisition function that maximizes the average predictive variance over all k classes for a sample. It computes the variance of class probabilities under a Bayesian posterior over model parameters and averages these variances, prioritizing points with high predictive dispersion across stochastic forward passes. This targets samples where the model’s class probability estimates are most unstable, indicating high epistemic uncertainty.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening lines describing '5. Mean Standard Deviation (MeanSTD) [29] maximizes the mean standard deviation of the predicted probabilities...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Mean Standard Deviation (MeanSTD) [29] maximizes the mean standard deviation of the pre-
topic_metadata.title: Clustering and CoreSet representative selection
topic_metadata.description: Representative/diversity-based strategies such as KMeans and CoreSet aim to select batches that approximate the overall data distribution in a feature space. KMeans iteratively chooses centroids proportional to squared distances from existing centroids, while CoreSet operates in the model’s penultimate layer h(x), repeatedly picking the point farthest from its nearest labeled neighbor. These methods view the selected points as a proxy for the full dataset, emphasizing coverage of the feature space.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.section_heading: Mean Standard Deviation (MeanSTD) [29] maximizes the mean standard deviation of the pre-
topic_metadata.title: Cluster-Margin for diverse low-confidence sampling
topic_metadata.description: Cluster-Margin combines clustering with margin-based uncertainty to choose diverse, low-confidence samples. It first performs hierarchical agglomerative clustering with average linkage to structure the unlabeled pool, then identifies points within clusters that have the lowest margin scores (least confident predictions). Finally, it filters these to a diverse subset of size b, differing from CoreSet by performing clustering only once as a preprocessing step.

topic_metadata.title: Weighted-sum combination and DPP balancing
topic_metadata.description: Weighted-sum optimization combines uncertainty and representativeness scores into a single acquisition value via α = α_uncertainty + β α_representative, but introduces a hyperparameter β and mismatched score formats (scalar vs matrix). Exploitation-Exploration is an example that subtracts a similarity term from entropy-based uncertainty to reduce redundancy while promoting diversity. DPPs are highlighted as a natural way to jointly account for per-sample uncertainty and pairwise diversity without extra hyperparameters, though exact sampling incurs O(N³) complexity.

topic_metadata.title: Two-stage combined selection strategies
topic_metadata.description: Two-stage (or multi-stage) optimization refines candidate sets sequentially using different criteria, often first selecting an informative subset and then enforcing diversity. WAAL first trains a discriminative network on labeled vs unlabeled data and then uses it for batch selection. BADGE computes gradient embeddings in the first stage and clusters them with KMeans++ in the second, whereas DBAL prefilters to the top ρb most uncertain points and then clusters them into b groups, choosing samples near cluster centers.

topic_metadata.title: Data-aspect enhancements: pseudo-labeling
topic_metadata.description: Data-aspect DAL enhancements use pseudo-labeling to exploit large unlabeled pools without explicit annotation. CEAL assigns pseudo-labels to high-confidence (low-entropy) predictions and includes them in subsequent training iterations, effectively enlarging the labeled set. This approach requires confidence thresholds as hyperparameters; poor tuning can introduce erroneous labels and harm performance.

topic_metadata.title: Loss function modification via adversarial objectives
topic_metadata.description: Altering the target model’s loss function is proposed as another route to enhancing DAL. WAAL introduces a min–max loss that leverages unlabeled data to better discriminate between labeled and unlabeled samples during training. This adversarial-style objective aims to shape the feature space so that selected unlabeled batches are both diverse and distributionally informative for label acquisition.

topic_metadata.title: Ensemble-based uncertainty: MC Dropout and ensembles
topic_metadata.description: Ensemble-based techniques counteract the overconfidence of softmax outputs by aggregating predictions from multiple stochastic models. MC Dropout interprets dropout at test time as approximate Bayesian inference, marginalizing over weight uncertainty via Monte Carlo integration to obtain predictive uncertainty; it behaves like an implicit ensemble of subnetworks. Beluch et al. empirically show that explicit ensembles of multiple independently trained classifiers often outperform MC Dropout for estimating uncertainty in DAL.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Compared deep active learning strategies
topic_metadata.description: The study compares 19 deep active learning methods, spanning random sampling, classic uncertainty-based heuristics (Entropy, Margin, LeastConf and their MC Dropout variants), Bayesian methods like BALD, and other uncertainty measures such as MeanSTD and VarRatio. It also includes pseudo-labeling and hybrid strategies like CEAL(Entropy), diversity-based and core-set-style methods such as KMeans and KCenter, gradient-based BADGE, adversarial query approaches (AdversarialBIM), and more complex frameworks like WAAL, VAAL, and LPL. This broad set enables a comprehensive comparison across different acquisition paradigms and modeling assumptions.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: GPU-accelerated KMeans for large pools
topic_metadata.description: To handle clustering over large unlabeled data pools, the authors replace the standard scikit-learn KMeans implementation, which is too time-consuming, with a GPU-based version implemented using the faiss library. This GPU-accelerated KMeans is used within DeepAL+ to make clustering-based DAL more scalable and better suited to deep learning workloads. It specifically targets the computational bottleneck of clustering in pool-based active learning on large-scale datasets.
topic_metadata.text_span: Continuation of 'DAL methods.' paragraph from “For KMeans, considering that we need to cluster large amounts of data…” through “…implemented KMeans with GPU (KMeans (GPU)) based on the faiss library [28].”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Common backbone and DAL toolkit
topic_metadata.description: All active learning methods share a common backbone model, ResNet18 without pre-training, to ensure a fair comparison across acquisition strategies. The experiments are run within the DeepAL+ toolkit, with consistent classifier settings applied to every DAL method. This controlled setup isolates the effect of the acquisition function from architectural or training differences in the underlying classifier.
topic_metadata.text_span: End of 'DAL methods.' paragraph starting from “For all AL methods, we employed ResNet18 (w/o pre-training)…” through “We run these experiments using DeepAL+ toolkit.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Experimental protocol and evaluation metrics
topic_metadata.description: Each experiment is repeated three times with different random splits of the initial labeled and unlabeled pools (controlled by a fixed seed), and results are averaged to reduce variance. Performance is summarized primarily via the area under the budget curve (AUBC), where the curve relates accuracy to labeling budget, with higher AUBC indicating better overall performance over the entire active learning process. The final accuracy after exhausting the labeling budget (F-acc) is also reported as a terminal performance metric. Additional implementation and dataset details are relegated to an appendix.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph under 'Experimental protocol.' from “We repeat each experiment for 3 trials…” through “More details of experimental settings… are in Section D in Appendix.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Task grouping for comparative analysis
topic_metadata.description: For analysis, the authors divide the tasks into three groups: standard image classification datasets, medical image analysis datasets, and a group for comparative studies involving MNIST and Waterbird. This grouping structures the interpretation of results by domain characteristics—conventional benchmarks, medical imaging, and tasks with specific comparative or spurious correlation concerns. It underpins how aggregate statistics like AUBC and F-acc are summarized and discussed across different problem types.
topic_metadata.text_span: Beginning of Section 3.2, from “For analyzing the experiment results, we roughly divided our tasks into three groups…” through the sentence enumerating the three groups.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty methods vs. random on benchmarks
topic_metadata.description: On standard image classification tasks, typical uncertainty-based strategies such as LeastConf, Margin, and Entropy (including CEAL) outperform random sampling by roughly 1–3% in average AUBC over the active learning process. However, paired t-tests on AUBCs across these methods reveal no single uncertainty-based approach is significantly better than the others, with all p-values above 0.05. This suggests that while uncertainty sampling helps over random, the precise uncertainty heuristic often does not critically affect performance on these benchmarks.
topic_metadata.text_span: Section 3.2 discussion from “The typical uncertainty-based strategies on group 1, standard image classification tasks…” through “…no method performs significantly better than the others (all p-value are larger than 0.05).”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Impact of MC Dropout on uncertainty
topic_metadata.description: For most standard image classification tasks, MC Dropout versions of uncertainty-based methods show negligible or even counter-intuitive differences compared to their non-dropout counterparts, aligning with earlier observations in the literature. TinyImageNet is an exception, where dropout-based variants outperform original methods by about 1–3% in AUBC. The authors hypothesize that relying on a single backbone’s feature representation yields less accurate uncertainty estimates on this harder dataset, while dropout increases predictive variability and better differentiates uncertainty among unlabeled samples. Thus, MC Dropout appears more beneficial when feature representations are less reliable or the task is more complex.
topic_metadata.text_span: Section 3.2 from “Considering dropout, there are only negligible effects…” through the explanation ending with “Therefore dropout versions provide better acquisition functions on TinyImageNet.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: CEAL threshold effects on performance
topic_metadata.description: The CEAL(Entropy) method, which augments entropy-based acquisition with pseudo-labeling of confident samples, improves over plain Entropy by about 0.5% on average across eight datasets when using a very small confidence/entropy threshold of 1e-5. While this indicates the approach can be effective, its gains depend sensitively on the choice of threshold. The authors stress that careful tuning of this hyperparameter is necessary to realize performance improvements from CEAL.
topic_metadata.text_span: Section 3.2 sentences starting from “Another comparison group is CEAL(Entropy) and Entropy…” through “This idea seems effective, but the threshold must be carefully tuned to get better performance.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Anomalous behavior on medical image tasks
topic_metadata.description: On medical imaging datasets such as Pneumonia-MNIST, some DAL methods perform worse than random sampling; for example, VarRatio underperforms Random by 4.5% in AUBC. The authors also observe that the final accuracy achieved by certain DAL strategies (e.g., KCenter) can exceed the accuracy obtained when training on the full labeled dataset, and that MC Dropout variants often do worse than their non-dropout versions (e.g., Entropy vs. EntropyD). These findings are labeled as abnormal phenomena, suggesting domain shift, data properties, or model–acquisition interactions in medical imaging may fundamentally alter how active learning behaves compared to standard benchmarks.
topic_metadata.text_span: Section 3.2 from “On medical image analysis tasks (e.g., PneumoniaMNIST), performances are slightly different; VarRatio is even 4.5% lower than Random.” through the sentence “These abnormal phenomena could be…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Distribution shift and redundancy in active learning
topic_metadata.description: The section attributes some of the observed performance behaviors in DAL experiments to distribution shift between training and test sets and to redundancy in the queried samples during active learning. Distribution shift can cause actively acquired labeled data to be unrepresentative of the test distribution, limiting generalization even when uncertainty criteria are optimized. Redundant acquisitions waste labeling budget on similar or overlapping samples, reducing the efficiency gains expected from active learning. Further technical analysis of these phenomena is deferred to an appendix section.
topic_metadata.text_span: Short narrative sentence following the table caption: 'caused by the distribution shift between training/test sets and data redundancy in AL processes. The detailed explanations are in Section E.1 in Appendix.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Limitations of representativeness/diversity-based DAL methods
topic_metadata.description: Representativeness/diversity-based methods such as KMeans, KCenter, and VAAL are evaluated and found not to show clear performance advantages over uncertainty-based measures. These methods incur substantial computational overhead: KMeans and KCenter repeatedly compute pairwise distance matrices over evolving feature representations, and VAAL requires retraining a variational autoencoder (VAE) each iteration. Large unlabeled pools (e.g., EMNIST) exacerbate memory consumption due to storing full distance matrices, leading to some experiments being infeasible. Thus, their theoretical appeal in diversity and coverage is tempered by practical time and memory costs.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Dependence of representativeness-based DAL on feature quality
topic_metadata.description: The authors note that representativeness-based active learning strategies perform well in classical machine learning settings but that their success in deep active learning hinges on the quality of learned feature representations. Poor or unstable features can undermine clustering or distance-based selection, leading to weaker gains from methods like KMeans and KCenter. This observation aligns with prior implicit analyses in the literature and is supported by the comparative results in the table. The section also highlights that a GPU-accelerated KMeans implementation is both more time-efficient and slightly better performing than a CPU version, emphasizing the role of scalable feature-space operations.

topic_metadata.title: Performance gains and instability of LPL
topic_metadata.description: The Loss Prediction Loss (LPL) method shows substantial improvements in final accuracy (F-acc) over full supervised training on several datasets such as SVHN, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and CIFAR10-imb. However, its performance is highly sensitive to hyper-parameters of the LossNet component, particularly the feature size determined by the fully connected layer, and it fails on more complex datasets like EMNIST and TinyImageNet despite extensive tuning. The difficulty is linked to predicting target loss in settings with many categories, but this can be mitigated by using a pre-trained backbone (e.g., pre-trained ResNet18), which provides better feature representations and substantially improves LPL’s effectiveness.

topic_metadata.title: WAAL limitations on many-class datasets
topic_metadata.description: Weighted Adversarial Active Learning (WAAL) exhibits similar failure patterns to LPL on datasets with many categories, such as EMNIST and TinyImageNet. topic_metadata.title: Marginal benefit and high cost of AdvBIM
topic_metadata.description: AdvBIM augments DAL training with adversarial samples, computed via an adversarial distance r for each unlabeled sample at every iteration, but does not achieve performance gains comparable to LPL. Because the adversarial examples are crafted using the current backbone model, the additional robustness they provide is limited, resulting in only marginal improvements. The method is extremely time-consuming and computationally prohibitive, to the point that experiments on large datasets like EMNIST and TinyImageNet could not be completed.

topic_metadata.title: WAAL robustness to epochs and diversity modeling
topic_metadata.description: In the ablation study, WAAL consistently outperforms Entropy and BADGE and is notably less sensitive to the number of training epochs, achieving stable AUBC (around 0.825) even with as few as 5 epochs and showing little change up to 30 epochs. The robustness is attributed to WAAL’s explicit modeling of diversity among samples and its use of unlabeled data to build better representations, which reduces data bias. This property is particularly attractive for DAL, as effective performance can be maintained with fewer training epochs, saving computation time.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Group-wise accuracy metrics on Waterbird
topic_metadata.description: The Waterbird dataset is partitioned into four groups based on bird type and background: {(waterbird, water), (waterbird, land), (landbird, land), (landbird, water)}. Besides overall accuracy, the study reports mismatch accuracy (for the spurious/background-mismatched groups {(waterbird, land), (landbird, water)}) and worst-group accuracy (the minimum accuracy among all four groups). These metrics quantify performance under distribution shift and group imbalance, revealing robustness and fairness properties of DAL methods.

topic_metadata.article_title: A comparative survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Enhancing techniques in LPL and WAAL
topic_metadata.description: LPL and WAAL use additional enhancing mechanisms—loss prediction and leveraging unlabeled-data information—to guide query selection in deep active learning. On Waterbird without pretraining, these techniques can outperform standard uncertainty or clustering-based methods in overall accuracy by extracting more informative signals from the data. However, both methods struggle on the worst group under both pretraining regimes, likely because group imbalance biases loss prediction and unlabeled-data statistics, harming performance on minority or hardest subgroups.

It notes that these methods do not generalize well across all tasks and stresses the need for more universal enhancement approaches. Cluster-Margin is cited as a method that scales active learning to very large batch sizes (100K–1M), illustrating both progress and the difficulty of surpassing such scalability.

Challenges and Future Directions of DAL
topic_metadata.title: Integrating DAL with Semi- and Self-Supervision
topic_metadata.description: There is a research trend toward combining deep active learning (DAL) with semi-supervised and self-supervised learning (S4L) to better exploit unlabeled data. Work by Chan et al. suggests that a significant portion of DAL's benefits can be absorbed by strong S4L techniques, based on extensive empirical comparisons. A key future direction is to design DAL pipelines that more effectively leverage unlabeled data in very low-label regimes.

Challenges and Future Directions of DAL
topic_metadata.title: Domain-Specific DAL in Autonomous Driving and Medicine
topic_metadata.description: DAL is proposed as a promising tool for data-insufficient, safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving and medical image analysis. In autonomous driving, active learning for nighttime detection of pedestrians and bicycles significantly improved mean average precision compared to manually selected training data. In medical imaging, the prevalence of rare but critical diseases and the high cost of expert annotation make class imbalance and rare-class emphasis central design concerns for DAL strategies. The text underscores that each domain has distinct requirements, motivating task- and domain-specific DAL research.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Labeling requirements for deep learning
topic_metadata.description: Due to their complex architectures and high capacity, deep learning models require large quantities of labeled samples for effective training. The availability of large-scale annotated datasets has therefore become a key enabler for DL performance. This creates a dependency between DL success and the cost and effort of obtaining high-quality labeled data.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Historical evolution of deep learning
topic_metadata.description: This topic covers the chronological development of deep learning models from early neural network formulations to modern deep architectures. It mentions the McCulloch-Pitts model, the introduction of backpropagation, the first RNNs, LeNet as an early DNN, Deep Belief Networks, and AlexNet’s breakthrough performance on ImageNet. It highlights how improvements in computing power and architectures led to superior results across visual, language, and speech tasks.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Data greed and labeling bottlenecks in DL
topic_metadata.description: The text emphasizes that DL’s recent breakthroughs depend heavily on massive labeled datasets, making it highly data-greedy. It explains that while unlabeled data are easy to obtain, manual annotation is costly, especially in expert domains such as COVID-19 lung lesion labeling, medical imaging, speech recognition, remote sensing, robotics, and specialized NLP tasks. This creates a practical bottleneck and motivates methods that maximize performance gains from a small number of labeled samples.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Active learning query scenario paradigms
topic_metadata.description: The section categorizes AL approaches by application scenario into membership query synthesis, stream-based selective sampling, and pool-based active learning. Membership query synthesis allows the learner to query labels for any point in input space, including synthetically generated samples. Stream-based selective sampling decides online for each incoming sample whether to query its label, whereas pool-based methods evaluate the entire unlabeled pool and select the best samples based on ranking. These paradigms define how and when label queries are made in practice.

topic_metadata.title: Convolutional Neural Network as baseline DL
topic_metadata.description: The section references a convolutional neural network (CNN) as a common deep learning model used as the baseline architecture when comparing DL, AL, and DeepAL. CNNs serve as the feature extractor and prediction model whose parameters are later adapted within the active learning process.

topic_metadata.title: Device resource constraints and AL strategy
topic_metadata.description: The text contrasts mobile devices, which require timeliness and have limited storage and computation, with larger devices that have ample resources. It notes that the commonly used pool-based sampling strategy in AL research is more suitable for large, resource-rich devices, implying that alternative strategies may be needed for constrained mobile platforms.

topic_metadata.title: Label budget and stopping conditions
topic_metadata.description: Both the pool-based AL cycle and the DeepAL workflow are described as iterative processes that terminate when a label budget is exhausted or when predefined stopping conditions are satisfied. This highlights the importance of explicitly modeling annotation cost (budget) and designing stopping strategies to decide when further querying is no longer beneficial.

topic_metadata.title: Importance of AL query rule design
topic_metadata.description: Active learning (AL) begins from unlabeled datasets and relies on carefully designed query rules to select the most informative samples for labeling. These rules aim to minimize labeling cost while maximizing model performance. Consequently, the quality and design of query rules are central to the overall effectiveness of AL methods, and there is extensive research focused on this aspect.

topic_metadata.title: Scalability to high-dimensional data
topic_metadata.description: Active learning methods face significant challenges when applied to high-dimensional data such as images, text, and video. Many existing approaches were developed and evaluated primarily on low-dimensional problems, limiting their direct applicability to complex, real-world domains. This scalability issue constrains the broader deployment of traditional AL techniques in modern deep learning settings.

topic_metadata.title: Feature extraction limitations in AL
topic_metadata.description: Traditional active learning typically operates on pre-extracted features and lacks the capability to learn feature representations jointly with querying. In contrast, deep learning models are designed, either manually or automatically, to perform high-performance feature extraction as part of end-to-end training. This gap means that classical AL frameworks often cannot fully exploit the representational power of deep models without additional integration mechanisms.

topic_metadata.title: Model uncertainty and overconfident softmax
topic_metadata.description: Uncertainty-based query strategies are central in Active Learning, but directly applying them to Deep Learning is problematic because DL models tend to be overconfident. The softmax output (Softmax Response, SR) is an unreliable confidence measure and can perform worse than random sampling when used for sample selection. This highlights a core challenge in using standard DL outputs for AL uncertainty estimation.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Batch Query Strategies for Deep AL
topic_metadata.description: Empirical work shows that traditional heuristic query strategies designed for one-by-one selection may fail when applied to deep learning in batch settings. Consequently, many researchers develop batch query methods that simultaneously optimize the information content and diversity of selected samples, better matching the training dynamics of deep models.

topic_metadata.title: Decomposition of DeepAL research components
topic_metadata.description: The DeepAL framework is decomposed into two core parts: active learning (AL) query strategies applied to the unlabeled dataset, and deep learning (DL) model training methods. Additional research axes include methods for improving model generalization and strategies for deciding when to stop querying. This decomposition structures the subsequent survey sections that analyze each component systematically.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Pool-based DeepAL optimization formulation
topic_metadata.description: In the pool-based setting, DeepAL defines an unlabeled dataset Uₙ with sample space X, label space Y, and joint distribution P(x, y), and a current labeled set Lₘ. Using a deep model f: X → Y, the goal is to design a query strategy Q that selects Lₘ ⊆ Uₙ to minimize the expected loss E(x,y)[ℓ(f(x), y)] while keeping m ≪ n. This formalizes DeepAL as choosing a minimal labeled subset that achieves a desired accuracy, highlighting that the query strategy Q is central to reducing labeling cost.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph beginning 'In the pool-based method, we define U_n = {X, Y}...' through Equation (1) and the following explanation of m ≪ n and labeling cost.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Acquisition function for batch selection
topic_metadata.description: Within BMDAL, the acquisition function a_batch(B, f_θ(L)) evaluates a candidate batch B of unlabeled samples given the current labeled training set L (also denoted D_train) and model f_θ. The optimal batch B* is defined as the subset of U that maximizes this acquisition score, formalizing batch selection as an arg max optimization over all possible subsets. This provides a general mathematical template under which specific batch criteria, such as uncertainty or diversity, can be instantiated.
topic_metadata.text_span: Equation (2) and accompanying explanatory sentences around 'In the context of BMDAL, at each acquisition step...' through 'In order to facilitate understanding, we also use D_train...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Redundancy issue in independent batch selection
topic_metadata.description: Constructing batches by independently selecting top-scoring samples can yield sets of highly similar, information-rich points that provide redundant information to the model. Such redundancy wastes labeling resources and does not significantly improve the model’s understanding of the data distribution. This motivates more sophisticated batch acquisition strategies that explicitly account for relationships and diversity among samples, beyond independent uncertainty scores.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final paragraph of subsection 3.1.1, beginning 'Clearly, however, this method is not feasible...' discussing similar samples and wasted labeling resources.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Exploration-P: balancing uncertainty and redundancy
topic_metadata.description: Exploration-P addresses limitations of early BMAL methods that over-rely on similarity and exploitation of boundary samples, leading to batches that poorly represent the feature-space distribution. It uses a deep neural network to learn feature representations, computes sample uncertainty via entropy, and aggregates uncertainty over a selected set S as E(S) = Σ E(xᵢ). Redundancy within S is quantified by R(S), a sum of pairwise similarities Sim(xᵢ, xⱼ) based on learned features and a similarity matrix M. The final objective I(S) = E(S) − α/|S|·R(S) promotes batches with high total uncertainty and low redundancy, explicitly trading off exploration and exploitation.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraphs starting with 'The performance of early Batch Mode Active Learning (BMAL)...' through the definitions of R(S) in Equation (6) and I(S) in Equation (7)

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Hybrid AL queries: uncertainty and diversity
topic_metadata.description: The section discusses hybrid active learning query strategies that explicitly weight uncertainty and redundancy/diversity within a mini-batch. A scalar α is introduced to balance these components, so that selected samples are both informative (high uncertainty) and non-redundant (diverse). This hybridization aims to improve the effectiveness of batch selection compared to using either criterion alone.
topic_metadata.text_span: Opening sentence: 'where, 𝛼 is used to balance the weight of the hybrid query strategies, uncertainty and redundancy.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Diverse Mini-Batch Active Learning (DMBAL)
topic_metadata.description: DMBAL augments K-means-based selection by weighting cluster optimization with sample informativeness, jointly considering information volume and diversity under a mini-batch query setting. It is designed to scale from generalized linear models to deep learning, enhancing both scalability and batch diversity. The method focuses on constructing diverse yet informative mini-batches for labeling.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences beginning 'Moreover, DMBAL (Diverse Mini-Batch Active Learning) [255] adds informativeness...' through '...increases the diversity of active query samples in the mini-batch.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Dataset-dependent suitability of AL strategies
topic_metadata.description: The text highlights that diversity-based and uncertainty-based query strategies do not suit all datasets equally, and their effectiveness depends on dataset statistics. Diversity-based methods perform better with richer category content and larger batch sizes, whereas uncertainty-based methods are preferable for smaller batches and less rich content. In BMAL settings with unfamiliar, potentially unstructured data, it is hard to pre-select the appropriate strategy.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting 'Although the above improvements have resulted in a good performance...' through '...makes it impossible to determine which AL query strategy is more appropriate.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Practical dominance of uncertainty-based querying
topic_metadata.description: Despite the superior performance of hybrid strategies, the text notes that uncertainty-based active learning remains widely used in deep learning. This is primarily because uncertainty measures integrate conveniently with softmax output layers, simplifying implementation. Thus, practical considerations still favor pure uncertainty sampling in many deep AL systems.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences 'Notably, although the hybrid query strategy achieves superior performance, the uncertainty-based AL query strategy is more convenient...' through 'Thus, the query strategy based on uncertainty is still widely used.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Bayesian neural network formulation for AL
topic_metadata.description: The section formalizes deep Bayesian active learning by defining a probabilistic neural network with parameters θ having a prior p(θ), usually Gaussian, and a softmax likelihood p(y=c|x,θ). It introduces the posterior p(θ|X,Y) via Bayes’ rule and the predictive distribution for a new point as an expectation over this posterior. This Bayesian formulation underpins uncertainty-aware acquisition functions in deep models.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting 'To solve the above problems, Deep Bayesian Active Learning appears...' through equations (8) and (9).

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: DBAL with BCNNs and MC-dropout
topic_metadata.description: DBAL [72] combines Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks with active learning, adapting the BALD acquisition function to high-dimensional deep learning settings. It models CNN weights with Gaussian priors and employs variational inference to approximate the posterior, while in practice MC-dropout is often used as a low-cost stochastic regularization technique to draw posterior samples. MC-dropout has been shown to be equivalent to variational inference in this context and yields good empirical performance on real datasets.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences from 'DBAL [72] combines BCNNs (Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks) [70] with AL methods...' through 'Moreover, this regularization technique has been proven to be equivalent to variational inference [71].'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Limitations and critiques of DBAL methods
topic_metadata.description: The text reports several critiques of DBAL-style approaches. A core-set method argues DBAL is unsuitable for large datasets due to its need for batch sampling, and another analysis claims that using dropout at test time yields performance similar to standard neural network softmax responses as uncertainty measures. Furthermore, DEBAL attributes DBAL’s overconfident predictions to pattern collapse in variational inference, motivating ensemble-based Bayesian active learning variants.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting 'However, a core-set approach [192] points out that DBAL [72] is unsuitable...' through '...DEBAL (Deep Ensemble Bayesian Active Learning) [165] argues that the pattern collapse phenomenon [211] in the variational inference method leads to the overconfident prediction characteristic of the DBAL method.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: ACS-FW Bayesian core-set optimization
topic_metadata.description: ACS-FW (Active Bayesian CoreSets with Frank-Wolfe optimization) reconstructs the batch structure in active learning to optimize a sparse subset that approximates the log-posterior of the full dataset. It uses the Frank–Wolfe algorithm, together with random projections, to select a Bayesian core set that scales to large data while retaining posterior fidelity. Compared with entropy- and BALD-based strategies, ACS-FW achieves better coverage of the overall data manifold.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph, sentences starting “Inspired by the latest research on Bayesian core sets [33, 99], ACS-FW…” through “…achieves better coverage across the entire data manifold.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Deep probabilistic ensembles for DBAL
topic_metadata.description: Deep Probabilistic Ensembles (DPEs) use a regularized ensemble of deep networks to approximate a deep Bayesian neural network. The method maintains multiple models whose diversity is controlled by regularization, and uses their predictive variability as a proxy for Bayesian uncertainty. DPEs are evaluated on large-scale visual active learning experiments to assess their classification performance and usefulness as uncertainty estimators.
topic_metadata.text_span: End of the first paragraph, beginning with “DPEs (Deep Probabilistic Ensembles) [39] introduces an expandable DPEs technology…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: ActiveLink for KG link prediction
topic_metadata.description: ActiveLink is a deep active learning framework for link prediction in knowledge graphs that adopts a Bayesian perspective on neural link predictors. It extends uncertainty sampling by exploiting the structural information of the knowledge graph, yielding a task-specific acquisition function. This method targets efficient querying in relational domains where links (triples) rather than independent instances are labeled.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences from “ActiveLink (Deep Active Learning for Link Prediction in Knowledge Graphs) [156] is inspired…” to “…thereby creating a novel DeepAL method.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Meta-learning-based unbiased incremental training
topic_metadata.description: ActiveLink addresses the bias introduced by naive incremental training in iterative active learning, where retraining from scratch is costly and simple fine-tuning overweights either new or early-selected data. In each AL iteration, it updates model parameters with newly selected samples and then approximates a meta-objective that anticipates future prediction performance based on previously selected samples. This meta-learning-based procedure balances the influence of new and past data, providing an approximately unbiased estimate of model parameters over the evolving labeled set.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences beginning with “ActiveLink further noted that although AL can sample efficiently…” through “…thereby to achieve an unbiased estimation of the model parameters.”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Core-set based density methods and FF-Active
topic_metadata.description: Density-based methods in deep active learning focus on selecting a core set of points that represents the overall data distribution, thereby reducing labeling cost while preserving coverage of the feature space. FF-Active implements this idea by performing farthest-first traversal in the neural activation space to pick diverse points, and is related to Exploration-P which uses early-stage random queries to improve exploration and avoid low-diversity traps. These approaches emphasize representativeness and diversity of the selected subset rather than pure uncertainty.
topic_metadata.text_span: Portion under heading “3.1.4 Density-based Methods”, from “The term, density-based method…” through the paragraph on “FF-Active (Farthest First Active Learning) [75]…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Discriminative Active Learning with density awareness
topic_metadata.description: Discriminative Active Learning (DAL) also frames active learning as a binary classification problem between labeled and unlabeled data, but explicitly aims to make the two sets indistinguishable. By sampling from the unlabeled pool in proportion to data density, DAL avoids overfocusing on sparse regions and instead reflects the true distribution more faithfully. The approach is conceptually general and can be transferred beyond standard classification tasks to other problem types.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph continuing from Active Palmprint Recognition, sentences starting “Similar to [56], DAL (Discriminative Active Learning) [79] also regards AL as a binary classification task…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Dataset characteristics, gradient analysis, and ensembles
topic_metadata.description: Gradient Analysis (GA) evaluates the relative importance of images in common datasets and serves as a general tool for understanding diversity and utility of training examples. Its findings show that some datasets exhibit nearly uniform sample importance, making small subsampling ineffective and cautioning against blindly using tiny sub-datasets in active learning. Additionally, comparative studies indicate that ensemble-based active learning can better handle class imbalance and produce more calibrated uncertainty estimates than Monte Carlo dropout–based Bayesian methods or density-based approaches.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph beginning “Furthermore, the attributes of the dataset itself also have an important impact…” through the sentences discussing GA [225] and ensemble-based AL [19].

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Standard Active Learning Pipeline Structure
topic_metadata.description: The standard AL pipeline is decomposed into three components: an oracle providing labeled data, a predictor (e.g., a Bayesian Neural Network) that learns from labeled data and outputs predictive uncertainty, and a guide that uses a fixed, hard-coded acquisition function. The acquisition function selects the next unlabeled sample to query, and this process repeats in cycles. This structure highlights the rigidity of traditional acquisition functions compared to adaptive approaches.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph beginning 'Fig.4 presents a comparison between traditional AL, RAL and DRAL pipelines. The pipeline of AL is shown in Fig.4a...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Reinforced Active Learning (RAL) with Policy BNN
topic_metadata.description: RAL replaces the fixed acquisition function in standard AL with a Bayesian policy network that learns a sampling policy via reinforcement learning. A BNN predictor produces probabilistic outputs, which are aggregated into a comprehensive probability distribution and passed to a BNN probabilistic policy network. This policy network receives oracle feedback each labeling round and updates the acquisition function to better select optimal query points for the current dataset.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraphs describing RAL starting with 'Accordingly, one good option may be to use reinforcement learning to dynamically tune the acquisition function. RAL (Reinforced Active Learning) [86] proposes...' and 'The pipeline of RAL (Reinforced Active Learning) [86] is shown in Fig.4b...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Deep Reinforcement Active Learning for Person Re-ID
topic_metadata.description: DRAL extends the reinforcement learning-based query strategy to the person re-identification task using a deep reinforcement active learning framework. For each query anchor (probe), an agent sequentially selects candidate instances from a gallery pool to be labeled by the oracle with binary feedback (positive/negative). The state encodes similarity relationships among instances, and rewards derived from oracle feedback guide the agent to adjust its querying policy to obtain high-quality samples.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraphs starting with 'DRAL (Deep Reinforcement Active Learning) [136] adopts a similar idea...' and ending with '...calculates rewards based on oracle feedback to adjust agent queries.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Active-iNAS: Joint Active Learning and NAS
topic_metadata.description: Active-iNAS challenges the assumption that a suitable deep learning model architecture is fixed prior to active learning and focuses on jointly optimizing both the model and the query strategy. It uses neural architecture search (NAS) to dynamically explore effective model architectures while actively selecting informative samples. This integration aims to find architectures that are particularly well-suited to the evolving labeled set in DeepAL, instead of relying on a predesigned model.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph beginning 'On the other hand, Active-iNAS (Active Learning with incremental Neural Architecture Search) [76] notices that most previous DeepAL methods...' through '...to dynamically search for the most effective model architectures while conducting active learning.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: SSAL multi-phase training across AL cycles
topic_metadata.description: SSAL proposes a semi-supervised active learning regime that orchestrates unsupervised, supervised, and semi-supervised training phases across AL iterations to maximize use of available data without increasing labeling cost. Before AL begins, labeled and unlabeled data are used for unsupervised pretraining; in each AL cycle, the model is first trained in a supervised manner on labeled data and then refined via semi-supervised learning on all data. This constitutes a new training methodology where different learning paradigms are systematically combined within the AL loop.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final part of the section, paragraph starting 'Unlike ARAL [146] and VAAL [204]...' through the detailed description of SSAL's training process.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Training methods and data utilization
topic_metadata.description: This topic highlights that exploring model training procedures and data utilization techniques in Deep Active Learning (DeepAL) can yield performance gains larger than merely changing query strategies. By better exploiting existing labeled and unlabeled data without increasing labeling cost, these methods mitigate the issue of having too few actively queried samples to effectively update deep models. It emphasizes optimizing how data is used in training rather than only focusing on which data to query.
topic_metadata.text_span: opening paragraph discussing 'exploration of training methods and data utilization skills' and 'full use of existing data'

topic_metadata.title: Two-stage uncertainty in deep models
topic_metadata.description: This topic explains why traditional uncertainty-based query strategies from shallow models are not directly applicable to deep learning models. A deep model is conceptualized as comprising a feature extraction stage and a task learning stage, each contributing its own uncertainty. Relying solely on the last-layer output underestimates the true predictive uncertainty, because it ignores uncertainty arising in earlier feature representations. The section introduces this two-stage uncertainty perspective, illustrated conceptually in Fig. 8.

topic_metadata.title: AL-MV multiview layer-based uncertainty
topic_metadata.description: AL-MV (Active Learning with Multiple Views) treats outputs from different hidden layers of a CNN as distinct views of the data. It explicitly models uncertainty at both the feature extraction and task learning stages by considering uncertainties from multiple intermediate layers. The algorithm adaptively weights the uncertainty from each layer to obtain a more accurate overall uncertainty estimate for sampling decisions. This multiview aggregation aims to improve query quality compared with using only the final layer.
