topic_metadata.title: Multilevel U-Net DeepAL for segmentation
topic_metadata.description: This topic describes a Deep Active Learning framework for finger bone segmentation built on Deeply Supervised U-Net. It uses outputs from multiple segmentation hidden layers together with the final layer output as inputs to the active learning component. These multilevel predictions are integrated to evaluate the 'information size' or informativeness of each sample for querying. By leveraging deep supervision and multi-scale features, the method refines uncertainty estimation for medical image segmentation tasks.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting 'Similarly, [254] uses a similar strategy to implement a DeepAL framework for finger bone segmentation tasks.' through '...basis for the evaluation of the sample information size.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Stabilizing Predictions (SP) stopping strategy
topic_metadata.description: The SP method proposes an AL stopping strategy based on prediction stability over an unlabeled 'stop set' drawn from the pool. At each iteration, the model’s predictions on this stop set are monitored, and querying stops once these predictions stabilize, under the assumption that a well-trained model exhibits stable outputs. This approach avoids extra annotation costs because the stop set remains unlabeled, aligning with the budget-conscious goals of active learning. Although introduced for AL in general, it is also applicable to DeepAL.
topic_metadata.text_span: Section 3.4 paragraphs beginning 'Although these stopping criteria are simple...' and 'Specifically, the SP predivides a part of the samples...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Query strategies for model uncertainty
topic_metadata.description: To address uncertainty in deep models within DeepAL, the survey highlights several query strategy families: uncertainty-based and hybrid methods, Deep Bayesian Active Learning (DBAL), and density-based techniques. These approaches aim to select informative samples by leveraging confidence scores, Bayesian uncertainty estimates, and data distribution structure. The table cites multiple works under each category, reflecting active research on optimizing query policies.
topic_metadata.text_span: Rows under 'Model uncertainty in Deep Learning' in Table 1, including 'Uncertainty-based and Hybrid Query Strategies', 'Deep Bayesian Active Learning (DBAL)', and 'Density-based Methods'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: AL criteria integrated into deep belief networks
topic_metadata.description: One line of work integrates active learning criteria directly into deep belief networks (DBNs) for classification. The combined system is then evaluated on various real uni-modal and multi-modal datasets, exploring how AL-driven sample selection interacts with DBN feature learning. This represents an early example of fusing deep generative models with AL strategies.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence beginning '[173] first integrated the criteria of AL into the deep belief network and subsequently conducted extensive research...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Active transfer learning for hyperspectral images
topic_metadata.description: Subsequent work on HSI classification combines active learning with transfer learning to mitigate cross-domain disparities. One approach uses AL to initialize the HSI labeling process and then performs transfer learning, recommending the construction and linking of higher-level features between source and target HSI data. Another proposes a unified deep network with active transfer learning to achieve strong classification performance with fewer labeled samples.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences beginning 'Similarly, [48, 133] also studied the classification of HSI...' through '...training the HSI classification well while using less labeled training data.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Committee-based DeepAL for object detection
topic_metadata.description: A DeepAL framework for object detection employs a layered architecture as a 'query by committee' to select images for annotation. The method also adopts an exploration–exploitation trade-off strategy, balancing querying highly uncertain examples with exploring diverse regions of the data space. This reduces labeling costs while training robust object detectors for domains such as autonomous driving and other real-world applications.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting with “[178] designs a DeepAL framework for object detection…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Transfer learning and AL for wildlife monitoring
topic_metadata.description: Deep neural networks are combined with transfer learning and active learning to identify and count species in camera trap imagery. For UAV-based wildlife detection, transfer sampling (TS) is introduced to locate corresponding regions between source and target datasets, enabling more effective domain transfer. Active sampling focuses labeling on informative or transferable regions, improving detector reusability across different environments while conserving annotation effort.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph describing works [154] and [110] on camera trap and UAV wildlife detection

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Self-paced DeepAL for pulmonary and bone segmentation
topic_metadata.description: DASL introduces Nodules R-CNN for pulmonary nodule segmentation, generating segmentation masks as examples and combining active learning with self-paced learning (SPL) to progressively select informative yet learnable samples, thus reducing labeling effort. A related Nodule-plus Region-based CNN extends this idea to 3D CT nodule detection and segmentation using a deep self-paced active learning (DSAL) strategy that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data. Deep-supervised active learning for finger bone segmentation iteratively fine-tunes the model and uses intermediate hidden-layer outputs as selection criteria, achieving comparable segmentation quality to full annotation with fewer labeled samples.
topic_metadata.text_span: Same medical segmentation paragraph from “DASL (Deep Active Self-paced Learning) [233]…” to the end mentioning finger bone segmentation [254]

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Active learning for visual imitation navigation
topic_metadata.description: In navigation tasks, imitation learning uses first-person visual observations and teacher actions to train a student agent to predict appropriate actions in its own environment. The system employs deep convolutional networks for feature extraction and imitation policy learning, and then integrates active learning to query additional samples where the model’s confidence is low. By selectively adding these uncertain examples to the training set, the navigation strategy is substantially improved using relatively few labeled demonstrations.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph under video processing describing the imitation learning navigation method [100]

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Curriculum-based active learning for translation
topic_metadata.description: A curriculum learning framework related to active learning controls which training samples are presented to a machine translation model over time. It dynamically chooses examples based on the estimated difficulty of each sample and the current competence of the model, effectively shaping the learning schedule. This adaptive curriculum improves training efficiency and yields notable accuracy gains, and its underlying idea informs richer sample selection strategies in DeepAL.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second machine translation paragraph discussing the curriculum learning framework [164]

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Addressing Sampling Bias in Active Text Classification
topic_metadata.description: [166] focuses on the sampling bias problem that arises in deep active text classification, where iterative selection can skew the labeled set. Using large-scale text corpora from [250], the work studies how AL strategies affect data distribution and classification performance. The methods generally outperform traditional AL baselines, indicating better handling of sampling bias in deep settings.
topic_metadata.text_span: Text classification subsection, sentences starting with “[166] focuses on the problem of sampling bias…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Active Deep Networks with RBMs for Sentiment
topic_metadata.description: [257] builds an Active Deep Network (ADN) using Restricted Boltzmann Machines to integrate unsupervised pretraining on both labeled and unlabeled data. Within a semi-supervised framework, active learning is used to jointly select labeled data and refine the classifier, exploiting large pools of unlabeled text. This yields competitive performance on sentiment classification by improving generalization with minimal labels.
topic_metadata.text_span: Semantic analysis subsection, paragraph describing ADN with RBMs and semi-supervised AL for sentiment classification

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: DeepAL for News Accuracy Detection
topic_metadata.description: [22] proposes a human-computer collaborative system for detecting misleading or false news content using deep active learning. The model operates with 1–2 orders of magnitude fewer labeled samples than fully supervised baselines, yet improves detection performance. Reduced annotation needs accelerate convergence and yield about 25% average performance gains in news accuracy detection.
topic_metadata.text_span: Semantic analysis subsection, sentences beginning with “[22] proposes a human-computer collaborative learning system…”

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: ALPNN for EEG Report Concept Extraction
topic_metadata.description: [141] introduces an Active Learning Policy Neural Network (ALPNN) to identify concepts and relationships in large collections of EEG (electroencephalogram) reports. The model actively selects which samples to annotate, improving extraction of clinical knowledge from semi-structured text. This supports scalable construction of clinical knowledge bases from EEG narratives.
topic_metadata.text_span: Information extraction subsection, sentences describing ALPNN for concepts and relationships in EEG reports [141]

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Online Active Learning for Open-Domain Dialogue
topic_metadata.description: [13] applies an online AL strategy to deep models for open-domain dialogue systems that interact with real users. The system incrementally learns from user feedback in each dialogue round, querying for information when most beneficial. This setup enables continual improvement of conversational quality with limited annotation overhead.
topic_metadata.text_span: Question-answering subsection, sentences about [13] using online AL for open domain dialogue with user feedback

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Hidden-Space Uncertainty for VQA Active Learning
topic_metadata.description: [104] observes that conventional AL strategies, which estimate uncertainty in the output space, can fail on tasks like Visual Question Answering (VQA) where multiple phrasings are correct. Output-based uncertainty can be overestimated, sometimes performing worse than random sampling. To address this, [104] proposes measuring uncertainty in the model’s hidden representation space, better handling paraphrasing and improving AL effectiveness for VQA generation.
topic_metadata.text_span: Question-answering subsection, sentences beginning with “[104] finds that AL strategies designed for specific tasks…” through the proposal to estimate uncertainty in the hidden space

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: MLFS: DeepAL for Gene and miRNA Selection
topic_metadata.description: MLFS (Multi-Level Feature Selection) [101] integrates deep learning and active learning to select genes and miRNAs based on expression profiles. The method performs multi-level feature selection while incorporating known biological relationships between miRNAs and genes. It is applied to miRNA expansion tasks, aiming to identify informative molecular features with fewer labeled experiments.
topic_metadata.text_span: Other applications subsection, sentences describing MLFS [101] for gene/miRNA selection and miRNA expansion

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Risk-Aware DeepAL for Robot Trajectories
topic_metadata.description: [8] introduces a risk-aware resampling technique that leverages active learning with deep models and existing solvers to optimize robot trajectories, particularly for collision avoidance in environments with moving obstacles. This approach reduces the cost of failure by focusing data collection on risky regions of the state space and is validated on a real nano-quadcopter. [258] further proposes an active trajectory generation framework for training a DNN-based inverse dynamics model, systematically designing informative trajectories for control learning.
topic_metadata.text_span: Other applications subsection, sentences covering risk-aware resampling [8] and active trajectory generation [258] for robot control

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: DALAUP for Anchor User Prediction
topic_metadata.description: DALAUP (Deep Active Learning for Anchor User Prediction) [37] presents a DeepAL framework for identifying anchor users in social networks. By actively selecting which users to label, the method reduces annotation cost while improving prediction accuracy for anchor users, who often link different platforms or communities. This supports more efficient social network analysis under label scarcity.
topic_metadata.text_span: Other applications subsection, sentences describing DALAUP [37] for anchor user prediction in social networks

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Early Research Stage of DeepAL
topic_metadata.description: Compared with traditional deep learning and active learning, DeepAL is characterized as being in a preliminary research stage. As a result, there are relatively few classic or foundational works, yet the paradigm is argued to have similarly broad application scenarios and practical value as standard deep learning methods.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences starting 'Compared with DL and AL, DeepAL is still in the preliminary stage of research...' through '...same broad application scenarios and practical value as DL.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Taxonomy of DeepAL Applications and Datasets
topic_metadata.description: To support access to concrete use cases, the survey classifies and summarizes DeepAL application scenarios and the datasets used across related work. These classifications are detailed in another section of the paper and compiled in a summary table, enabling readers to see how DeepAL has been instantiated across different domains and data resources.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences starting 'In addition, in order to facilitate readers’ access...' through 'The specific information is shown in Table 2.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Variability in random sampling baselines
topic_metadata.description: The performance of the random sampling baseline (RSB) in DeepAL experiments varies substantially across studies, even under seemingly identical settings. For instance, using 20% labeled CIFAR-10 data, RSB performance reported in one study is 13% higher than in another; similarly, under 40% labeled CIFAR-100 with VGG16 as feature extractor, reported results differ by 8%. These discrepancies complicate fair comparison of DeepAL methods and highlight sensitivity to experimental choices.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Conflicting findings on AL strategies
topic_metadata.description: Studies report conflicting conclusions regarding the relative effectiveness of diversity-based, uncertainty-based, and random sampling strategies in DeepAL. Some work claims diversity-based querying consistently outperforms uncertainty-based methods and that uncertainty-based approaches can even underperform RSB, while more recent research disputes this hierarchy. This inconsistency raises questions about how robust these strategy comparisons are to datasets, architectures, and experimental setups.
topic_metadata.text_span: second paragraph: 'Furthermore, the latest DeepAL research also exhibits some inconsistencies...' through '...shows that this is not the case.' and 'Compared with AL’s strategic selection of high-value samples, RSB has been regarded as a strong baseline...'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Role of ablation and transfer experiments
topic_metadata.description: Ablation studies and transfer experiments are proposed as necessary tools for understanding and validating DeepAL improvements. Ablation experiments help isolate which components or modifications are responsible for observed performance gains, while transfer experiments test whether an active learning strategy can reliably select high-value samples across different datasets. Together, these methods support more principled development and assessment of DeepAL algorithms.
topic_metadata.text_span: third paragraph: 'On the other hand, adequate ablation experiments and transfer experiments are also necessary...' through '...enable the indiscriminate selection of high-value samples for the dataset.'

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Hybrid supervised and unsupervised training schemes
topic_metadata.description: Training optimization in deep active learning increasingly focuses on integrating labeled datasets, unlabeled datasets, and generated data (e.g., via GANs) within a unified training scheme. This includes hybrid training methods that combine unsupervised, semi-supervised, and supervised learning throughout the active learning cycle. Such approaches are expected to produce larger performance gains than changing the selection strategy alone, by better exploiting all available data types.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph, sentences describing optimization of training methods with labeled/unlabeled data, GAN-based data expansion, and hybrid unsupervised/semi-supervised/supervised learning across the AL cycle.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Leveraging unlabeled and generated data
topic_metadata.description: Unlabeled and synthetically generated datasets are used to compensate for the scarcity of labeled examples in deep learning and the limited number of labeled samples selected by active learning. By exploiting these additional data sources, models can make fuller use of available information without incurring extra annotation costs. This helps mitigate the dependency of deep models on large labeled training sets.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph, sentences stating that these training methods address the need for many labeled samples, limited labeled selection in AL, and the benefits of unlabeled or generated datasets for reducing annotation costs.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Limits of over-reducing labeled subsets
topic_metadata.description: The text warns against blindly striving to train models on ever smaller labeled subsets. In datasets with high content variety and many samples, the relative difference in importance between individual samples may be negligible, reducing the benefit of aggressive subset minimization. This implies that extreme reduction of labeled data can undermine performance gains expected from active learning.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences cautioning that blindly pursuing training on smaller subsets is unwise and explaining the near-ignorable relative difference in sample importance for some large, diverse datasets.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Mixed improvement strategies for DeepAL
topic_metadata.description: There is no inherent conflict between advances in query strategies, training schemes, task independence, and computational efficiency, so combining these directions into mixed improvement strategies is advocated. Such integrated approaches can jointly reduce labeling costs and broaden application scenarios for DeepAL. Nonetheless, the field is characterized as still being in its infancy, indicating substantial room for future development.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final sentences of the section mentioning lack of conflict between improvement directions, importance of mixed improvement strategies, and overall assessment of DeepAL’s practical value and immaturity.

topic_metadata.article_title: A survey of deep active learning
topic_metadata.title: Query Strategy Optimization in DeepAL
topic_metadata.description: This topic focuses on designing and comparing query strategies tailored to deep neural networks within active learning. It includes uncertainty-based, diversity-based, and representativeness-aware sampling methods that select the most informative unlabeled instances for annotation. The optimization problem typically trades off informativeness, redundancy, and computational cost in the context of large-scale deep models.
topic_metadata.text_span: summary paragraph, second sentence (phrase: 'query strategy optimization')

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Pool-based versus stream-based active learning
topic_metadata.description: Traditional pool-based active learning assumes a fixed pool of unlabeled observations from which instances are selected for labeling, a setting that may not match dynamic real-world environments. In contrast, stream-based (online) active learning continuously receives data in a stream and must decide, on arrival, whether to query each observation. This online setting allows real-time adaptation to changing data distributions but also imposes sequential decision and resource constraints.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, sentences contrasting pool-based active learning with online/stream-based active learning

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Survey gap in online active learning
topic_metadata.description: Existing surveys either focus on pool-based active learning or on online learning from data streams under the assumption that all labels are available. Apart from a prior review centered on fuzzy-model-based online active learning, recent developments in broader online active learning methods have not been synthesized. This creates a gap for scenarios where labels are scarce or expensive in streaming contexts, motivating the need for this survey.
topic_metadata.text_span: Second paragraph, discussion of prior surveys (Aggarwal et al., Settles, etc., Lughofer 2017, Lu et al., Tieppo et al., Lima et al., Hoi et al.) and their limitations

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Terminology: stream-based AL vs selective sampling
topic_metadata.description: The text clarifies that some authors use a narrow definition of stream-based active learning focused purely on selecting informative stream observations for model fitting. Under this view, deciding which observations to query during prediction time is termed online selective sampling. The survey adopts a broader perspective, encompassing all methods that select informative data points to label from a data stream in an online manner.
topic_metadata.text_span: Middle of second paragraph, sentences defining stream-based active learning versus online selective sampling (Hanneke & Yang, 2021)

topic_metadata.title: Active learning scenarios in data streams
topic_metadata.description: This topic covers the different deployment scenarios in which stream-based active learning operates, such as fully supervised streams, partially labeled streams, and evolving environments with concept drift. Each scenario imposes constraints on how often labels can be queried, how quickly models must adapt, and what assumptions can be made about data distribution. These scenario distinctions guide the design of suitable active querying strategies.
topic_metadata.text_span: Middle of the paragraph: '...an overview of the main active learning scenarios...'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey

topic_metadata.title: Classification of online active learning approaches
topic_metadata.description: This topic focuses on taxonomies and classification schemes for organizing online active learning methods for data streams. Approaches may be grouped by query strategy (e.g., uncertainty-based, density-based), model type (single vs. ensemble), handling of concept drift, or label budget management. Such a classification helps compare methods, identify gaps, and structure the state-of-the-art landscape.
topic_metadata.text_span: Middle of the paragraph: 'Section3 represents the core of the review, with a brief overview of how online active learning approaches have been classified...'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey

topic_metadata.title: Evaluation strategies and performance metrics
topic_metadata.description: This topic concerns how to evaluate stream-based active learning algorithms, including metrics and protocols tailored to evolving data and limited labels. It involves assessing predictive performance over time (e.g., prequential accuracy), label efficiency, adaptation to concept drift, and computational cost, often under streaming evaluation setups. Appropriate evaluation strategies are critical to fairly compare algorithms and understand trade-offs between accuracy and labeling cost.
topic_metadata.text_span: Beginning and middle of the paragraph: section heading and 'In Sect.4, we examine evaluation strategies for online active learning algorithms.'

topic_metadata.title: Synthesis of methods and future research
topic_metadata.description: This topic addresses summarizing existing online active learning methods and outlining future research directions. It involves comparing methodological families, identifying common design patterns, and highlighting open problems such as more robust drift-aware querying, better integration with semi-supervised learning, or improved evaluation standards. Such synthesis guides subsequent work in the field.
topic_metadata.text_span: Later part of the paragraph: 'Section6 provides a summary of the most common online active learning methods and highlights potential directions for future research.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Supervised learning problem formulation
topic_metadata.description: Supervised learning is framed as learning a function that maps input variables (covariates) to an output variable (response). This function is estimated from a labeled dataset consisting of many input–output pairs. The focus is on using these labeled examples to train predictive models for tasks such as classification or regression.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph, sentences 1–3 of section 2

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Motivation for active learning usage
topic_metadata.description: Active learning is motivated by scenarios where obtaining labels is difficult, costly, or impractical for all available data. Under a labeling budget constraint, only a subset of unlabeled observations can be queried. Properly selected labeled subsets can enable classification or regression models to reach performance comparable to using all labels, while using only a small fraction of the available observations.
topic_metadata.text_span: First paragraph, sentences 4–8 of section 2

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Margin-based query strategies
topic_metadata.description: Margin-based active learning focuses on selecting instances that lie close to the current decision boundary of the classifier, where prediction uncertainty is highest. By querying labels for these borderline points, the learner aims to refine the boundary most efficiently, improving classification performance with fewer labeled examples. This strategy is often used with margin-based models such as SVMs or linear classifiers.
topic_metadata.text_span: The initial bullet describing a 'based query strategy, where data points close to the decision boundary are selected (Roth & Small, 2006; Balcan et al., 2007)'.

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Diversity and density-based selection
topic_metadata.description: Diversity- and density-based methods exploit structural information in the data to select instances that are both representative of the underlying distribution and diverse from already labeled points. Techniques include using Mahalanobis distance to find observations far from labeled samples, clustering to pick cluster representatives, and graph-based methods to model relationships among labeled and unlabeled instances. Semi-supervised strategies such as label propagation on graphs can guide the selection of influential or poorly propagated nodes to label.
topic_metadata.text_span: Bullet point 'Diversity- and density-based approaches. These methods exploit the structural information of the instances...' including examples with Mahalanobis distance, clustering, and graph-based / label propagation methods (Ge, 2014; Cacciarelli et al., 2022a; Nguyen & Smeulders, 2004; Min et al., 2020; Ienco et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2020b; Long et al., 2008).

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Hybrid active learning strategies
topic_metadata.description: Hybrid strategies combine multiple selection criteria to exploit complementary strengths, such as uncertainty, diversity, and representativeness. For example, one can first partition the input space via clustering and then apply margin-based sampling within each region to pick the most uncertain representative instances. These methods aim to balance local informativeness with global coverage of the data distribution.
topic_metadata.text_span: Bullet point 'Hybrid strategies. These are active learning algorithms that combine multiple instance selection criteria...' including the example combining margin-based sampling with clustering (Donmez et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2014).

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Macro scenarios of active learning
topic_metadata.description: Active learning methods are organized into three macro scenarios based on how unlabeled instances are provided to the learner and how queries are formed. This categorization abstracts over specific query strategies to emphasize the flow of information, the interaction with the oracle, and the constraints on which instances can be queried. Understanding these scenarios helps practitioners choose suitable active learning setups and compare algorithms fairly across different application contexts.
topic_metadata.text_span: Paragraph starting with '2.2 Active learning scenarios Active learning can be broadly categorized into three macro scenarios...' up to 'In the next subsections, each of the three macro scenarios will be discussed.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Batch size selection in active learning
topic_metadata.description: In pool-based active learning, the batch size k (number of instances labeled per iteration) governs how frequently the model is retrained and how many new instances are added. Smaller k allows more frequent updates of the selection criteria, but risks higher computational cost due to repeated training. Larger k, as in adding fixed percentages of the dataset, is more practical for large models where retraining is expensive, but increases the risk of redundant labeling. Thus, k embodies a problem- and model-specific trade-off between computational efficiency and avoiding redundant labels.
topic_metadata.text_span: From 'This allows a timely update of the instance selection criteria...' down to '...trade-off between computational efficiency and the risk of querying redundant labels.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Uncertainty-based acquisition in pool-based AL
topic_metadata.description: Pool-based active learning methods often rely on uncertainty-based instance selection, where candidate data points are scored by how uncertain the model is about their labels. These criteria are operationalized through acquisition functions, which map model predictions to informativeness scores. Combining uncertainty measures with acquisition functions like entropy, mutual information, or variation ratio enables more principled selection of instances whose annotations are expected to be most beneficial. This framework links model predictive distributions with label-query decisions.
topic_metadata.text_span: From 'To enhance pool-based active learning, many approaches combine uncertainty-based instance selection criteria with acquisition functions...' to '...for which the predictions are the most uncertain.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Mutual information and variation ratio criteria
topic_metadata.description: Beyond entropy, mutual information and variation ratio are alternative acquisition metrics derived from model predictions. Mutual information captures the expected reduction in uncertainty about model parameters or predictions after observing a label, emphasizing instances that can most change the model. Variation ratio measures how frequently the most probable class appears across predictions (e.g., in ensembles or Bayesian samples), with lower ratios indicating higher uncertainty. These measures help select a diverse set of highly uncertain points, complementing pure entropy-based selection.
topic_metadata.text_span: From 'Acquiring examples with the highest uncertainty is one way...' through '...in order to seek a diverse set of data points for which the predictions are the most uncertain.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Real-time sampling in manufacturing
topic_metadata.description: In chemical and manufacturing processes, a learner predicts product quality under strict time constraints for sampling decisions, often to preserve traceability in high-volume production. Online active learning selects which process observations to label in real time so that models for quality prediction, predictive maintenance, and visual inspection can be continuously updated. The key entities are production batches or items, quality measurements, time windows for decision-making, and evolving predictive models.
topic_metadata.text_span: Bullet point starting '• Chemical or manufacturing processes.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Sequential decisions in streaming media and trials
topic_metadata.description: For video streaming platforms and clinical trials, users or patients arrive sequentially and cannot be accumulated into a large candidate pool. Online active learning must decide on the fly whether to label or enroll each arriving subject or interaction to optimize learning or trial outcomes. This involves trade-offs between information gain, user or patient burden, and strict timing or recruitment constraints.
topic_metadata.text_span: Bullet point starting '• Video streaming and clinical trials.'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: NLP text classification with online AL
topic_metadata.description: In text classification tasks such as sentiment analysis and spam detection, data points like messages or documents arrive continuously. Online active learning frameworks decide in real time which texts to label so that the model can be updated incrementally and maintain or improve accuracy. Entities include incoming text streams, labeling actions, and continuously refined classifiers.
topic_metadata.text_span: Bullet point starting '• Text classification: In NLP...'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Unsupervised preprocessing in semi-supervised learning
topic_metadata.description: One category of semi-supervised methods is unsupervised preprocessing, which applies techniques such as dimensionality reduction, clustering, or feature extraction to the combined labeled and unlabeled dataset before supervised training. This transformation aims to produce a representation where informative samples are easier to identify and model parameters are better estimated when few labels are available. In online active learning, this includes using pre-trained networks to extract salient features from unlabeled instances prior to initiating the sampling routine, thereby guiding more informative query choices.
topic_metadata.text_span: final paragraph beginning 'Semi-supervised learning approaches can be distinguished into three categories...' through the example 'Rožanec et al. (2022) used a pre-trained network to extract salient features...'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Autoencoders for online active learning
topic_metadata.description: An autoencoder is trained on all available unlabeled data to learn a compressed representation that improves downstream online active learning. In this setting, the learned features are then used with linear regression models to enhance prediction and query selection under streaming conditions. This exploits the structure of unlabeled data without requiring additional labels.
topic_metadata.text_span: Opening sentence referencing Cacciarelli et al. (2022a)

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Wrapper methods with pseudo-labels
topic_metadata.description: Wrapper methods rely on one or more supervised learners trained jointly on labeled data and pseudo-labeled unlabeled data. Two core variants are self-training, using a single model that assigns pseudo-labels to confidently predicted examples, and co-training, where multiple models exchange their most confident predictions to generate pseudo-labels for each other. These methods integrate semi-supervised learning into the active learning loop.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences starting 'Wrapper methods, on the other hand...' through the description of co-training

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Pseudo-labels and confirmation bias risk
topic_metadata.description: Pseudo-labels help exploit unlabeled data in label-scarce environments but can induce confirmation bias. When models trust their own or peers’ pseudo-labels too strongly, they may reinforce early mistakes, degrading performance. Managing this risk is crucial when incorporating pseudo-labeled data into active learning pipelines.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence beginning 'Pseudo-labels can be very beneficial...' discussing confirmation bias from self-created labels

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Confirmation bias in active query strategies
topic_metadata.description: In a broader active learning context, confirmation bias refers to query strategies that preferentially select examples supporting the current model hypothesis. Such selection neglects challenging or contradictory instances that could drive model improvement, leading to overconfident yet brittle models. Designing acquisition functions that avoid this bias is critical for robust learning.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentence starting 'In the more general active learning framework, confirmation bias might also refer...'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Graph-based regularization and sampling
topic_metadata.description: Graph-based methods construct a graph over all data points and train a supervised model with a loss combining standard supervised terms and a regularization that enforces similar predictions for connected nodes. In online active learning, the graph encodes similarity relationships that guide query selection, such as choosing points in low-density regions or far from existing labeled examples. This couples semi-supervised smoothness assumptions with structure-aware active sampling.
topic_metadata.text_span: Final sentences beginning 'Finally, graph-based methods construct a graph...' through the end of the section

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.section_heading: Stationary data stream classiﬁcation approaches. These methods are designed to tackle
topic_metadata.title: Industrial quality control as stationary stream
topic_metadata.description: Industrial quality control is presented as an example where data streams can be treated as stationary due to controlled operating conditions. Control actions at regular intervals and continuous maintenance of system components stabilize the process, leading to relatively consistent data distributions. Stationary stream classification methods can leverage this stability to monitor product quality and detect anomalies with fewer assumptions about distribution shifts.
topic_metadata.text_span: middle of the section: 'such as quality control in industrial processes... continuous maintenance of the components of the system (Bisgaard & Kulahci, 2011)'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.section_heading: Stationary data stream classiﬁcation approaches. These methods are designed to tackle
topic_metadata.title: Human activity recognition from wearable data
topic_metadata.description: Human activity recognition using wearable devices is described as another application of stationary data stream classification. Data from sensors on fitness trackers or similar devices generates a continuous stream representing activities like walking, running, or sleeping, assumed to be relatively stable in distribution over time. Models can be updated in real time as new labeled examples arrive, enabling continuous personalization and improvement of activity classification.
topic_metadata.text_span: final sentences of the section: 'Another example is represented by human activity recognition using wearable devices... the model can be updated in real-time as new labeled examples become available (Miu et al., 2015)'

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.title: Real-time intrusion detection under cyberattack drift
topic_metadata.description: This topic focuses on real-time intrusion detection systems that monitor computer networks and must detect emerging forms of cyberattacks. Because attack patterns evolve, the underlying data distribution shifts, requiring classification models that adapt over time to maintain detection performance in streaming network data.
topic_metadata.text_span: Sentences 3 and 5 of the paragraph in this section

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.section_heading: Experimental design and bandit approaches. These methods, mostly related to regression
topic_metadata.title: Random sampling versus specialized strategies
topic_metadata.description: This topic contrasts naive random sampling with more advanced online active learning strategies. Random sampling selects instances from the data stream uniformly for annotation, ignoring informativeness. In contrast, specialized strategies target scenarios where labeling resources are limited or costly and where the data distribution may be non-stationary, requiring informed, adaptive selection to maintain model performance over time.
topic_metadata.text_span: paragraph beginning 'This categorization provides a comprehensive overview...' and discussing random sampling and specialized strategies under resource constraints and non-stationarity

topic_metadata.article_title: Active learning for data streams: a survey
topic_metadata.section_heading: Experimental design and bandit approaches. These methods, mostly related to regression
topic_metadata.title: General framework and drift adaptation
topic_metadata.description: This topic refers to a general framework that captures the main components shared across online active learning algorithms, with configurable options highlighted via callouts. The framework encompasses processes such as instance selection, querying, and model update in a streaming context. It also interfaces with drift detection and adaptation mechanisms that monitor changes in data distribution and trigger model adaptation, as detailed in referenced flowcharts.
